definition_zh: 在室内；在屋里；往室内
definition_en: inside a building rather than outside it
core_image: 雨水敲着窗，人缩在屋顶下的屋子里
scene: 外面下着冷雨，孩子们把球收进屋里。It is too cold to play outdoors, so we stay indoors all afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 indoors 是「在室内」（第 1 个义项：位于建筑物之内而不是户外）；句意是天太冷不适合在外面玩，所以我们整个下午都待在屋里。

pos.zh: 副词：在室内；在屋里
名词（作定语用）：室内的

forms.label: 无变化（副词无词形变化）

derivatives.zh: 由 in 加 door 构成，去掉副词词尾 -s，义为「室内的」
反义构词，out 加 door 再加 -s，义为「在户外」
由 indoors 去掉 -s 得到，用于修饰名词，如室内泳池

senses.title: Inside a building
senses.definition: in or into a building, not in the open air
senses.definitionCN: 在某座建筑物之内，不在露天地带
senses.example: The children were kept indoors by the heavy rain.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨让孩子们只好待在屋里。
senses.why: In plus door plus s: the word literally places you within the doors of a house.
senses.whyCN: in 加 door 再加 s，这个词字面上就是把人放在房屋的门之内。

senses.title: Moving into a building
senses.definition: used with a verb of movement to mean into a building
senses.definitionCN: 与表示移动的动词连用，表示进入建筑物内部
senses.example: Let us go indoors before it gets dark.
senses.exampleCN: 天黑之前我们进屋去吧。
senses.why: The same form covers both being in and going in, so the verb decides the direction.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形式既表示「在里面」也表示「进去」，方向由动词决定。

senses.title: Happening under a roof
senses.definition: taking place inside a building, such as sport or work
senses.definitionCN: 指运动、工作等在建筑物内部进行
senses.example: Most of the matches are played indoors in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 冬季大部分比赛都在室内进行。
senses.why: Once inside is the norm, the word describes any activity sheltered by a roof.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「在里面」成为常态，这个词就用来描写任何被屋顶遮蔽的活动。

senses.title: Avoiding the weather
senses.titleCN: 为了躲避天气而留在屋里
senses.definition: staying in because of rain, cold or heat
senses.definitionCN: 因为下雨、寒冷或炎热而留在室内
senses.example: We stayed indoors during the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨期间我们一直待在室内。
senses.why: The word often carries a reason: the weather outside is what pushes you in.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常带原因：外面的天气正是把人往里推的东西。

intro.en: Indoors is a late compound of in and door, with an adverbial -s added to mark place, much like besides and towards.
intro.cn: indoors 是 in 与 door 的晚期合成词，再加上副词性的 -s 表示地点，类似 besides、towards 的构法。

items.en: In was a preposition of place and dur came from Latin through Germanic for door.
items.cn: in 是古英语中表示位置的介词，而 door 经日耳曼语源自拉丁语的「门」。

items.en: English began to form phrases such as in door to describe being within a house.
items.cn: 中古英语开始使用 in door 这类短语，表示身处房屋之内。

items.en: The phrase in doors was written together and an adverbial -s was added to mark location.
items.cn: 短语 in doors 被写成一个词，并加上副词性的 -s 以标示地点。

items.en: Indoors settled into its present adverb role in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.
items.cn: indoors 在十八、十九世纪固定为今天的副词用法。

items.en: The adjective indoor was back-formed from it to modify nouns such as pool and game.
items.cn: 形容词 indoor 由它反推而来，用来修饰 pool、game 这样的名词。

note.en: The look-alike group holds compounds built on in; the near-meaning group holds words for being inside sheltered space.
note.cn: 形近组收以 in 为基础的合成词；近义组收表示身处遮蔽空间内部的词。

entries.definition: Inside a building, used before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「室内的」，是 indoors 去掉 -s 的形式。

entries.definition: Outside a building, in the open air.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在户外」，与 indoors 正好相反。

entries.definition: Away from the sea, towards the middle of a country.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或副词，义为「内陆的、向内陆」，只是拼写相近，词源不同。
副词或介词，义为「在里面」，比 indoors 更宽泛。
短语，义为「在家」，强调自己的住所。

entries.definition: Protected from wind, rain or danger.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有遮蔽的」，强调受保护。

normalIntro.en: The hooks work from the parts in and door, the adverb ending, and the everyday contrast with out.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从 in 与 door 两个部分、副词词尾以及与 out 的日常对照入手。

normal.en: In doors means inside the doors, so the plural door is the whole house.
normal.cn: in doors 就是「在门里面」，那扇门的复数就是整座房子。

normal.en: The -s ending is the same adverbial -s seen in towards and afterwards.
normal.cn: 词尾 -s 与 towards、afterwards 里的副词 -s 是同一个。

normal.en: Drop the -s and you get the adjective indoor, which must stand before a noun.
normal.cn: 去掉 -s 就得到形容词 indoor，它只能放在名词前面。

normal.en: Stay indoors is the most common pairing, used with weather as the cause.
normal.cn: stay indoors 是最常见的搭配，天气常是它的原因。

normal.en: Swap in for out and you get outdoors, the open air version of the same idea.
normal.cn: 把 in 换成 out 便得到 outdoors，同一想法在露天的版本。

abstract.en: A house is a wall drawn around the word in, and indoors is the angle of standing inside that wall.
abstract.cn: 房子是围绕 in 画的一堵墙，indoors 就是站在墙内的那个角度。

abstract.en: To be indoors is to be held by a roof; the sky is replaced by a ceiling.
abstract.cn: 身处室内就是被屋顶托住，天空换成了天花板。

abstract.en: Every indoors hides a door: shelter is always something you entered and can leave.
abstract.cn: 每个 indoors 里都藏着一扇门：遮蔽总是你走进来、也能走出去的东西。

examples.en: The children stayed indoors because of the rain.
examples.cn: 因为下雨，孩子们待在屋里。

examples.en: Let us go indoors and have some tea.
examples.cn: 我们进屋喝杯茶吧。

examples.en: All the plants are grown indoors during the winter.
examples.cn: 冬天所有植物都在室内培育。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因兜子」——因为外面冷，兜子一罩，人就留在屋里了。

root: 由 in（在……之内）与 door（门）合成，加副词性 -s 表示地点；同族词有 indoor、outdoors。

sensesIntro.en: From the plain location inside the doors, indoors spreads to entering, to sheltered activity and to staying in against bad weather.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「在门里面」这一基本位置出发，indoors 延伸到进入、在遮蔽下进行的活动，以及为躲坏天气而留在屋里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing inside the closed doors of a house.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在房屋关着的门里面。

branches.en: PLACE LINE: the body is within the walls.
branches.cn: 位置线：身体在四壁之内。

branches.en: MOTION LINE: a verb of movement pushes the body in.
branches.cn: 运动线：移动动词把人推进去。

branches.en: ACTIVITY LINE: games and work take place under the roof.
branches.cn: 活动线：运动与工作在屋顶下进行。

branches.en: WEATHER LINE: rain and cold explain the staying in.
branches.cn: 天气线：雨和冷解释了为什么留在屋里。

branches.en: SHELTER LINE: the door frame marks protection from the open air.
branches.cn: 遮蔽线：门框标出与露天的分界，带来保护。

intro.en: A compound of a preposition and a noun, plus an old adverbial ending that marks place.
intro.cn: 由介词与名词合成的词，再加一个标示地点的古老副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The parts are Germanic, but door itself goes back to a Latin word for door, and Latin foris gives English foreign.
latinIntro.cn: 构词成分属日耳曼语，但 door 可追溯到拉丁语的「门」；拉丁语 foris 则给了英语 foreign。

definition_zh: 工业的；产业的；工业化的
definition_en: relating to industry, to factories and to the making of goods
core_image: 一排排厂房冒着白烟，机器在轰鸣
scene: 城市的边缘聚集着厂房与货仓。The old industrial area has been turned into a park.
sceneCN: 这里 industrial 是「工业的」（第 1 个义项：与工业和工厂有关）；句意是那片旧工业区已经被改成了公园。

pos.zh: 形容词：工业的；产业的；工业发达的
名词（复数）：工业股票；工业公司

forms.label: 无变化（形容词无词形变化）

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词根 industri- 加名词后缀构成，义为「工业；行业；勤奋」
由 industrial 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使工业化」
由 industrialize 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「工业化」
同根形容词，加 -ious，义为「勤劳的」

senses.title: Relating to factories
senses.definition: connected with factories and the making of goods in large numbers
senses.definitionCN: 与工厂以及大批量制造商品有关
senses.example: Industrial waste must be treated before it leaves the plant.
senses.exampleCN: 工业废料在出厂之前必须经过处理。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the noun industry to whatever it describes.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把名词 industry 挂到它所修饰的对象上。

senses.title: Having many industries
senses.definition: having a strong economy based on factories and manufacturing
senses.definitionCN: 经济以工厂与制造业为基础的
senses.example: The north of the country is heavily industrial.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家的北部高度工业化。
senses.why: A place can be filled with industry, so the adjective describes its character.
senses.whyCN: 一个地方可以被工业填满，于是这个形容词也描述它的性质。

senses.title: Of a whole sector
senses.titleCN: 产业的：指整个行业层面
senses.definition: belonging to an entire branch of production rather than one workshop
senses.definitionCN: 属于整个生产门类，而不是单个作坊
senses.example: The report looks at industrial policy across the region.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告考察整个地区的产业政策。
senses.why: From single factories the word rises to the level of policy and sectors.
senses.whyCN: 从单个工厂出发，这个词上升到政策和行业层面。

senses.title: Of the machine age
senses.definition: belonging to the period when machines replaced handwork
senses.definitionCN: 属于机器取代手工劳动的那个时期
senses.example: The industrial age changed how people lived and worked.
senses.exampleCN: 工业时代改变了人们的居住与工作方式。
senses.why: Industrial also names an era, because factories reorganized all of life.
senses.whyCN: industrial 也命名一个时代，因为工厂重组了整个生活。

intro.en: Industrial is the adjective of industry, which comes from Latin industria, meaning diligence, the quality of working hard.
intro.cn: industrial 是 industry 的形容词形式，而 industry 来自拉丁语 industria，意为「勤勉」，即努力工作的品质。

items.en: Industria was built from indu, or in, plus struere, to build.
items.cn: industria 由 indu（或 in）加 struere（建造）构成。

items.en: The sense was activity or diligence, and it could also name a trade.
items.cn: 其义为活动或勤勉，也可指一门行业。

items.en: Industrie reached English through French with both senses kept.
items.cn: industrie 经法语进入英语，两种含义都被保留。

items.en: During the eighteenth century industry came to mean manufacturing at scale.
items.cn: 十八世纪 industry 开始指大规模的制造业。

items.en: The adjective industrial was formed to describe everything factories touched.
items.cn: 形容词 industrial 被造出来，描述工厂所触及的一切。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words sharing the industria root; the near-meaning group holds adjectives for factories and working life.
note.cn: 形近组收共享 industria 词根的词；近义组收与工厂和劳动有关的形容词。

entries.definition: The making of goods in factories, or a trade.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「工业；行业；勤奋」，是工业一词根的名词。
形容词，义为「勤劳的」，只是拼写相近，含义偏向勤奋。
形容词，义为「已工业化的」，由 industrialize 变来。

entries.definition: The business of making goods in factories.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「制造业」，强调制造过程。
形容词，义为「商业的」，强调买卖而非生产。
形容词，义为「机械的」，强调机器运转本身。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the industria root, the -al adjective ending and the familiar phrase industrial revolution.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 industria 词根、形容词后缀 -al 以及熟悉的短语 industrial revolution。

normal.en: Industry plus -al gives an adjective: whatever is industrial belongs to industry.
normal.cn: industry 加 -al 得到形容词：industrial 修饰的东西都属于工业。

normal.en: Industria meant diligence in Latin, so industry first meant hard work, then the work itself.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 industria 意为勤勉，所以 industry 先指努力，再指所做的事。

normal.en: Industrialize adds -ize to make a verb, so a country can be industrialized.
normal.cn: industrialize 加上 -ize 成了动词，所以说一个国家可以工业化。

normal.en: Industrial area and industrial waste both say what the word describes.
normal.cn: industrial area 与 industrial waste 都说明了这个词描述的是什么。

normal.en: Do not confuse industrial with industrious: factories against hardworking people.
normal.cn: 不要把 industrial 与 industrious 混淆：一个是工厂，一个是勤劳的人。

abstract.en: Industry is diligence made visible: pipes, chimneys and night shifts.
abstract.cn: 工业是看得见的勤勉：管道、烟囱与夜班。

abstract.en: Industrial is a scale word, not a place word; it describes eras and policies.
abstract.cn: industrial 是尺度的词，不是地点的词；它描述时代与政策。

abstract.en: Smoke is the quickest picture: wherever it rises in rows, the word fits.
abstract.cn: 烟是最快的画面：凡成排升起之处，这个词就用得上。

examples.en: The industrial part of the city is grey with smoke.
examples.cn: 城市的工业区被烟雾染成灰色。

examples.en: Industrial growth brought jobs to the small town.
examples.cn: 工业增长给这个小镇带来了工作。

examples.en: They studied industrial design at a technical college.
examples.cn: 他们在一所技术学院学习工业设计。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬打湿」——厂房里的机器硬打湿了工人的衣服。

root: 拉丁语 industria（勤勉）= indu/in（在内）+ struere（建造）；同族词有 industry、industrious、industrialize。

sensesIntro.en: From the diligence inside industria, industrial grows into an adjective for factories, for regions full of them, for whole sectors and for a historical age.
sensesIntro.cn: 从 industria 中的勤勉之义出发，industrial 发展为描述工厂、工业密集的地区、整个产业以及一个历史时代的形容词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rows of chimneys working through the night.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排排烟囱通宵工作。

branches.en: FACTORY LINE: waste, machines and goods belong to the plant.
branches.cn: 工厂线：废料、机器与货物都属于厂区。

branches.en: REGION LINE: a whole area can be filled with industry.
branches.cn: 地区线：整片区域可以被工业填满。

branches.en: SECTOR LINE: policy looks at the industry as a whole.
branches.cn: 产业线：政策着眼于作为整体的产业。

branches.en: TIME LINE: the machine age gets its name from the same root.
branches.cn: 时间线：机器时代也从同一词根得名。

branches.en: OUTPUT LINE: what a factory and a sector produce is one flow of goods.
branches.cn: 产出线：工厂与产业生产的东西是同一条货物流。

intro.en: An adjective built on a Latin noun, with suffixes that make verbs and nouns from it.
intro.cn: 一个建立在拉丁名词之上的形容词，并由此再生出动词与名词形式。

latinIntro.en: The root struere, to build, also yields structure and construct, which is why industria means diligence.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 struere 意为建造，也产生了 structure 与 construct，这也是 industria 意为勤勉的原因。

definition_zh: 使工业化；实现工业化
definition_en: to develop factories and large-scale production in a country or area
core_image: 田野旁立起新的厂房，烟囱冒出第一缕烟
scene: 一个农业小镇，几年间盖起了工厂。The government wanted to industrialize the poor region within a decade.
sceneCN: 这里 industrialize 是「使工业化」（第 1 个义项：使某地发展起工业）；句意是政府想用十年时间让这个贫困地区实现工业化。

pos.zh: 动词：使工业化；使产业化
不及物：实现工业化

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -ation，义为「工业化」
去掉动词词尾，义为「工业的」
加表人后缀 -ist，义为「工业家」
词根名词，义为「工业；行业」

senses.title: To bring industry to a place
senses.definition: to build factories and manufacturing in a place that had little of them
senses.definitionCN: 在原本缺少工业的地方建立工厂与制造业
senses.example: The plan was to industrialize the southern provinces.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划是要让南方各省工业化。
senses.why: The verb is simply industry made into an action: causing industry to exist.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词就是把 industry 变成动作：促使工业存在。

senses.title: To change production by machines
senses.definition: to replace handwork with machines and factory organization
senses.definitionCN: 用手工改为机器与工厂组织
senses.example: Farming in the valley was industrialized after the railway came.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路到来之后，山谷里的农业实现了工厂化。
senses.why: Not only countries but whole kinds of work can be pushed into factories.
senses.whyCN: 不只是国家，整类劳动也能被推进工厂体制。

senses.title: To become industrial
senses.definition: to develop into an industrial economy, used without an object
senses.definitionCN: 不带宾语时，表示自身发展成为工业经济
senses.example: The country industrialized faster than its neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家比邻国更快实现了工业化。
senses.why: When the change happens by itself, the verb drops its object.
senses.whyCN: 当变化自行发生时，动词就省掉了宾语。

senses.title: To be organized like a factory
senses.titleCN: 被像工厂那样组织起来
senses.definition: to make an activity standardized, large and machine-run
senses.definitionCN: 使某项活动标准化、大规模化、机器化
senses.example: Some critics say the school has been industrialized.
senses.exampleCN: 一些批评者说这所学校已经被工厂化了。
senses.why: The metaphor extends beyond economics into any activity made mechanical.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻超出经济领域，延伸到任何被机械化的活动。

intro.en: Industrialize is a modern verb built from industrial, itself from Latin industria, with the productive suffix -ize.
intro.cn: industrialize 是近代动词，由 industrial 加能产后缀 -ize 构成，而 industrial 又出自拉丁语 industria。

items.en: Industria meant diligence, built on indu, or in, plus struere, to build.
items.cn: industria 意为勤勉，由 indu（或 in）加 struere（建造）构成。

items.en: The word reached English as industrie, meaning skill or a trade.
items.cn: 这个词以 industrie 的形式进入英语，意为技艺或行业。

items.en: Industry came to name large-scale manufacturing in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 十八世纪 industry 开始指大规模制造。

items.en: -ize, from Greek through Latin, was added to industrial to make the action.
items.cn: -ize 经拉丁语源自希腊语，被加到 industrial 上构成动作。

items.en: Industrialize spread in the nineteenth century as nations pushed to build factories.
items.cn: 十九世纪各国争相建厂，industrialize 随之流行。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the industrial family; the near-meaning group holds verbs of economic change.
note.cn: 形近组收 industrial 一词族；近义组收描述经济变化的动词。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「工业化」，是 industrialize 的名词形式。
形容词，义为「工业的」，是动词的来源。
形容词，义为「勤劳的」，只是同根而含义不同。

entries.definition: To bring up to date with new methods.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使现代化」，与工业化常同时发生。

entries.definition: To replace human work with machines.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使机械化」，强调机器替代人手。

entries.definition: To grow or make something grow bigger.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「发展」，是更宽泛的说法。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the -ize ending, the family of nouns and adjectives, and the picture of a country changing.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 -ize 词尾、同族名词形容词以及一个地区转变的画面。

normal.en: Take industrial, add -ize, and the adjective turns into a verb of change.
normal.cn: industrial 加 -ize，形容词就变成表示变化的动词。

normal.en: The noun form swaps -ize for -ization, so the process is industrialization.
normal.cn: 名词形式把 -ize 换成 -ization，过程就是 industrialization。

normal.en: Newly industrialized is common: it names countries that changed in recent decades.
normal.cn: newly industrialized 很常见，指近几十年才转变的国家。

normal.en: The verb can drop its object: a country can simply industrialize.
normal.cn: 这个动词可以省略宾语：一个国家可以自行工业化。

normal.en: The industria root still means diligence, so the word is hard work raised to a national scale.
normal.cn: industria 词根仍是勤勉，所以这个词是放大到国家尺度的努力。

abstract.en: Industrialize is a before and after word: fields on one side, chimneys on the other.
abstract.cn: industrialize 是一个前后对比的词：一边是田野，一边是烟囱。

abstract.en: To industrialize a thing is to make it run like a factory, even a school or a farm.
abstract.cn: 把某样东西工业化，就是让它像工厂一样运转，哪怕是一所学校或一片农场。

abstract.en: Every -ize verb carries an engine: it makes something happen to what follows.
abstract.cn: 每个 -ize 动词都带着一台发动机：它让后面的对象发生改变。

examples.en: The country began to industrialize after the war.
examples.cn: 这个国家在战后开始工业化。

examples.en: They hoped to industrialize the region without destroying its forests.
examples.cn: 他们希望在不破坏森林的前提下使该地区工业化。

examples.en: Cheap coal helped the area industrialize quickly.
examples.cn: 廉价的煤帮助这一地区迅速实现工业化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬打湿来子」——机器硬干活打湿了衣衫的来子，工厂就这样建起来。

root: industrial（工业的）+ -ize（使……化）；industrial 出自拉丁语 industria（勤勉）。

sensesIntro.en: Industrialize starts as bringing factories to a place and widens to mechanizing any work, to the self-driven change of a country and even to the factory-like ordering of daily life.
sensesIntro.cn: industrialize 起初指把工厂带到一个地方，随后扩展到使任何劳动机械化、一个国家自行转变，乃至把日常生活按工厂方式组织起来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first chimney rising beside a rice field.
core.cn: 核心意象：稻田旁升起第一根烟囱。

branches.en: PLACE LINE: factories are brought into a region.
branches.cn: 地点线：工厂被带进一片区域。

branches.en: MACHINE LINE: handwork gives way to machines.
branches.cn: 机器线：手工让位于机器。

branches.en: ECONOMY LINE: the change happens on its own, without an object.
branches.cn: 经济线：变化自行发生，不带宾语。

branches.en: SYSTEM LINE: anything can be run like a factory.
branches.cn: 系统线：任何事物都能像工厂那样运作。

branches.en: PRODUCTION LINE: factories and machines together remake output.
branches.cn: 生产线：工厂与机器合起来重塑产出。

intro.en: A verb made with the productive -ize suffix on top of the industrial family.
intro.cn: 一个在 industrial 词族之上用能产后缀 -ize 构成的动词。

latinIntro.en: -ize comes from Greek -izein through Latin -izare, found in countless English verbs of change.
latinIntro.cn: -ize 经拉丁语 -izare 源自希腊语 -izein，出现在大量表示变化的英语动词中。

definition_zh: 工业；产业；行业；勤奋
definition_en: the making of goods in factories, a branch of trade, or steady hard work
core_image: 一片厂区里机器不停，工人在流水线旁忙碌
scene: 城市的经济账全写在一个个行业里。The car industry provides thousands of jobs in this region.
sceneCN: 这里 industry 是「行业、产业」（第 1 个义项：生产商品的一个门类）；句意是汽车产业在这个地区提供了数千个工作岗位。

pos.zh: 名词：工业；产业；行业；勤奋

derivatives.zh: 加 -al 构成形容词，义为「工业的」
加 -ious 构成形容词，义为「勤劳的」
加动词后缀构成，义为「使工业化」
加 -ist 构成，义为「工业家」

senses.title: A branch of production
senses.definition: a particular branch of trade or manufacturing
senses.definitionCN: 贸易或制造业的一个门类
senses.example: The steel industry has shrunk in recent years.
senses.exampleCN: 钢铁行业近年来萎缩了。
senses.why: The Latin word first named a kind of activity, so any organized trade counts as one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语此词原指一类活动，因此任何有组织的行业都算一种。

senses.title: Factories as a whole
senses.definition: the whole system of factories and manufacturing in a country
senses.definitionCN: 一国工厂与制造业的整体系统
senses.example: Industry grew quickly after the railway opened.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路开通后工业迅速增长。
senses.why: Bring the branches together and they form one large system, also called industry.
senses.whyCN: 把各个门类合起来就是一个大系统，同样叫 industry。

senses.title: Steady hard work
senses.definition: the quality of working hard and steadily
senses.definitionCN: 努力而持续工作的品质
senses.example: She was praised for her industry and patience.
senses.exampleCN: 她的勤奋与耐心受到称赞。
senses.why: This is the oldest Latin sense, and it survives beside the modern commercial ones.
senses.whyCN: 这是最早的拉丁语义，与近代商业义并存至今。

senses.title: A group of companies
senses.definition: the companies themselves, seen as a group with shared interests
senses.definitionCN: 指作为整体的企业群体，有共同利益
senses.example: Industry has asked the government to cut taxes.
senses.exampleCN: 企业界已要求政府减税。
senses.why: By a short step the activity names the people who carry it out.
senses.whyCN: 再走一小步，这项活动就用来命名从事它的人。

senses.title: Busy effort
senses.definition: constant effort in any kind of work, not only paid work
senses.definitionCN: 在任何工作中持续的努力，不限于有报酬的工作
senses.example: Her industry in the garden kept the family fed.
senses.exampleCN: 她在园子里的辛劳让全家不愁吃。
senses.why: The sense of diligence stretches beyond factories to any steady effort.
senses.whyCN: 勤勉之义超出工厂，延伸到任何持续的努力。

intro.en: Industry comes from Latin industria, diligence, built from indu, or in, and struere, to build.
intro.cn: industry 来自拉丁语 industria（勤勉），由 indu（或 in）与 struere（建造）构成。

items.en: Industria meant diligence, activity and effort, with no commercial colour at first.
items.cn: industria 意为勤勉、活动与努力，起初并无商业色彩。

items.en: The word also named a craft or trade, that is, the work itself.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语中，此词也指技艺或行业，即事情本身。

items.en: Industrie entered English from French with both diligence and trade in its meaning.
items.cn: industrie 经法语进入英语，兼有勤勉与行业两义。

items.en: In the eighteenth century industry shifted to large-scale manufacturing.
items.cn: 十八世纪 industry 转向指大规模制造业。

items.en: The plural industries became the normal way to name separate branches.
items.cn: 复数 industries 成为指称各个门类的常用形式。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the industria family; the near-meaning group holds words for trades and for hard work.
note.cn: 形近组收 industria 词族；近义组收行业与勤奋两方面的近义词。

entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「工业的」，是 industry 的形容词。
形容词，义为「勤劳的」，专指人勤奋。

entries.definition: To build factories in a place.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使工业化」，由本词根构成。

entries.definition: Trade and the companies that do it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「商业；生意」，比 industry 更宽泛。

entries.definition: The making of goods in factories.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「制造业」，只是 industry 的一个部分。
名词，义为「勤勉」，与 industry 的第三义项最近。

normalIntro.en: The hooks join the root meaning of diligence to the modern meaning of factories and trades.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把词根的勤勉之义与近代的工厂行业之义连起来。

normal.en: Industry once meant diligence only, so industrious still means hardworking.
normal.cn: industry 最初只表示勤勉，所以 industrious 至今仍是勤劳的。

normal.en: Heavy industry and light industry split the whole system by weight of goods.
normal.cn: 重工业与轻工业按货品的重量把整个体系一分为二。

normal.en: The plural industries names separate branches, such as film or steel.
normal.cn: 复数 industries 指彼此分开的门类，如电影业与钢铁业。

normal.en: Industry without an article usually means the whole productive sector.
normal.cn: industry 不带冠词时通常指整个生产部门。

normal.en: -al makes the adjective and -ous makes the personal quality, from one root.
normal.cn: -al 造形容词，-ous 造人品性词，都出自同一个词根。

abstract.en: Industry is diligence turned into machinery, work that never stops.
abstract.cn: 工业是勤勉化成机器，是不停歇的劳动。

abstract.en: One word holds both a factory and a virtue, because both mean sustained effort.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时装着工厂与美德，因为二者都意味着持续的努力。

abstract.en: Branches of industry are streams from one spring of organized labour.
abstract.cn: 各个行业都是从同一眼有组织劳动的泉里分出的溪流。

examples.en: The tourist industry is important to this island.
examples.cn: 旅游业对这座岛很重要。

examples.en: He owes his success to hard work and industry.
examples.cn: 他把成功归功于努力与勤勉。

examples.en: New industries have grown up along the coast.
examples.cn: 沿海一带兴起了新的产业。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因挡着锤」——工人因挡着就要锤，锤声不断就是工业。

root: 拉丁语 industria（勤勉）= indu/in（在内）+ struere（建造）；同族词有 industrial、industrious、industrialize。

sensesIntro.en: From the Latin sense of diligence, industry splits into a single trade, the whole factory system, the companies themselves and finally any steady effort.
sensesIntro.cn: 从拉丁语的勤勉出发，industry 分裂为单个行业、整个工厂体系、企业界，最后回到任何持续的努力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a factory line running all day beside busy workers.
core.cn: 核心意象：流水线整日运转，工人忙碌不停。

branches.en: TRADE LINE: one branch, such as steel or film.
branches.cn: 行业线：例如钢铁或电影这样的单个门类。

branches.en: SYSTEM LINE: all factories together make up industry.
branches.cn: 体系线：所有工厂合起来构成工业。

branches.en: VIRTUE LINE: diligence survives from the oldest Latin sense.
branches.cn: 美德线：勤勉从最古老的拉丁语义留存下来。

branches.en: PEOPLE LINE: the trade names the companies that run it.
branches.cn: 人群线：行业用来指经营它的企业。

branches.en: EFFORT LINE: hard work in any field, paid or not.
branches.cn: 努力线：任何领域里的辛勤，无论是否有报酬。

intro.en: A Latin noun that became one of the busiest word families in modern English.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁名词，成为近代英语中最活跃的词族之一。

latinIntro.en: The root struere, to build, also gives structure and construct, tying industry to building.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 struere（建造）也产生 structure 与 construct，把工业与建造连在一起。

definition_zh: 不可避免的；必然的；照例必有的
definition_en: certain to happen and impossible to avoid or prevent
core_image: 一辆停不下来的车，正朝路中央的人滑去
scene: 雨下了整整一周，河水一点点漫上堤岸。Floods were inevitable after such heavy rain.
sceneCN: 这里 inevitable 是「不可避免的」（第 1 个义项：必然发生、无法阻止）；句意是这么大雨之后洪水不可避免。

pos.zh: 形容词：不可避免的；必然的；照例必有的
名词（常作 the inevitable）：必然发生的事

derivatives.zh: 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「不可避免地」
加名词后缀 -ity，义为「必然性」
去掉否定前缀 in-，义为「可避免的」，较少使用
同出拉丁词根 evitare，义为「逃避；回避」

senses.title: Certain to happen
senses.definition: sure to happen, so that no plan can stop it
senses.definitionCN: 一定会发生，任何计划都无法阻止
senses.example: Another price rise now seems inevitable.
senses.exampleCN: 眼下又一次涨价看来不可避免。
senses.why: In- says no and evitare says avoid, so the word means simply not able to be avoided.
senses.whyCN: in- 表示「不」，evitare 表示「避免」，合起来就是「无法避免」。

senses.title: Unavoidable in doing something
senses.definition: unavoidable because of the nature of an activity
senses.definitionCN: 因为活动的性质而免不了
senses.example: Mistakes are inevitable when you learn a new language.
senses.exampleCN: 学一门新语言时出错是免不了的。
senses.why: Obligations come with roles, so the adjective describes what any actor must face.
senses.whyCN: 义务随角色而来，于是这个形容词描述每个行动者必然面对的事。

senses.title: A regular, expected thing
senses.definition: happening so regularly that it can be expected every time
senses.definitionCN: 规律性地发生，几乎每次都能预料到
senses.example: The inevitable questions came at the end of the talk.
senses.exampleCN: 报告结束后照例来了那些问题。
senses.why: When something always happens, people call it inevitable even without strict logic.
senses.whyCN: 当某事总是发生，即使没有严格逻辑，人们也称它必然。

senses.title: The thing that must come
senses.titleCN: 必然发生的事（名词用法）
senses.definition: the event that cannot be stopped, used with the
senses.definitionCN: 与 the 连用，指无法阻止的那件事
senses.example: We waited for the inevitable: the factory would close.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在等那件必然的事：工厂会关门。
senses.why: An adjective used with the turns into a noun naming the expected event.
senses.whyCN: 形容词与 the 连用就变成名词，指那件预料中的事。

senses.title: Unavoidable in a logical sense
senses.definition: following necessarily from the premises, as in an argument
senses.definitionCN: 在论证中从前提出发必然推出
senses.example: Given those two facts, the conclusion is inevitable.
senses.exampleCN: 有了那两条事实，结论就是必定的。
senses.why: The sense moves from physical prevention to logical necessity.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项从物理上的阻止不了，转向逻辑上的必然。

intro.en: Inevitable joins the Latin negative in- to evitabilis, avoidable, from evitare, to shun or avoid.
intro.cn: inevitable 由拉丁否定前缀 in- 与 evitabilis（可避免的）合成，后者出自 evitare（避开、避免）。

items.en: Evitare meant to shun or get out of the way, built on ex plus vitare, to avoid.
items.cn: evitare 意为躲开、让路，由 ex 加 vitare（避开）构成。

items.en: Evitabilis, avoidable, added the adjective suffix to the verb stem.
items.cn: evitabilis（可避免的）在动词词干后加了形容词后缀。

items.en: The negative form passed through French into English in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 否定形式在十五世纪经法语进入英语。

items.en: Inevitable first described things no one could escape, then moved into ordinary speech.
items.cn: inevitable 起初描述无人能逃脱之事，后来进入日常口语。

items.en: The looser sense of regular and expected grew in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪又生长出「照例必有」这一较宽松的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words in the evitare family; the near-meaning group holds words for certainty.
note.cn: 形近组收 evitare 词族的词；近义组收表示确定性的词。

entries.definition: In a way that cannot be avoided.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「不可避免地」，是 inevitable 加 -ly。

entries.definition: The quality of being certain to happen.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「必然性」，加 -ity 构成。
动词，义为「逃避」，与原词根 evitare 同源。
形容词，义为「无法避免的」，是更直白的同义词。
形容词，义为「确定的」，语气比 inevitable 弱。
形容词，义为「逃不掉的」，强调无处可逃。

normalIntro.en: The hooks pull the word apart into in, evitare and -able, then tie it to everyday cases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把词拆成 in、evitare 与 -able 三部分，再与日常情形挂钩。

normal.en: In- means not, evitare means avoid, and -able means can, so the word means cannot be avoided.
normal.cn: in- 表示不，evitare 表示避免，-able 表示能够，合起来就是无法被避免。

normal.en: Evade is the same root without the prefix, so to evade is to try to avoid.
normal.cn: evade 是去掉前缀的同一词根，所以 evade 就是设法躲开。

normal.en: Drop -ly from inevitably and you are back at the adjective.
normal.cn: 从 inevitably 去掉 -ly 就回到这个形容词。

normal.en: It is inevitable that is a fixed frame followed by a clause.
normal.cn: it is inevitable that 是一个固定框架，后面接从句。

normal.en: The inevitable is the adjective turned noun, meaning the expected event.
normal.cn: the inevitable 是形容词变名词，指那件预料中的事。

abstract.en: Inevitable is a door that has already closed before you reach it.
abstract.cn: inevitable 是一扇在你走到之前就已经关上的门。

abstract.en: The word pictures the absence of an exit, not the presence of a force.
abstract.cn: 这个词的画面是没有出口，而不是有一股力量。

abstract.en: What we call inevitable often simply means too late to change.
abstract.cn: 我们称作必然的东西，常常只是「已经来不及改变」。

examples.en: Some delay was inevitable during the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨期间有些延误是不可避免的。

examples.en: It is inevitable that people will disagree.
examples.cn: 人们意见不同是必然的。

examples.en: She accepted the inevitable and moved to a smaller flat.
examples.cn: 她接受了那件必然的事，搬进了一间更小的公寓。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬喂它包」——硬喂它包子也堵不住嘴，事情还是必然发生。

root: 拉丁否定前缀 in-（不）+ evitabilis（可避免的），后者出自 evitare（避开）；同族词有 inevitably、inevitability、evade。

sensesIntro.en: From the plain sense of no exit, inevitable widens to what any role entails, to whatever happens every time, to the expected event itself and to logical necessity.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「没有出口」这一本义出发，inevitable 扩展到角色必然带来的事、每次都会发生的事、预料中的那件事本身，以及逻辑上的必然。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road with no turn-off before the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条在墙前没有任何岔口的道路。

branches.en: CERTAINTY LINE: nothing human can stop it.
branches.cn: 确定线：人力无法阻止。

branches.en: ROLE LINE: what a task itself brings along.
branches.cn: 角色线：任务本身带来的东西。

branches.en: HABIT LINE: whatever turns up every time.
branches.cn: 习惯线：每次都出现的东西。

branches.en: EVENT LINE: the adjective becomes the expected thing.
branches.cn: 事件线：形容词变成那件预料中的事。

branches.en: NECESSITY LINE: from no escape to no other conclusion.
branches.cn: 必然线：从逃不开走向没有别的结论。

intro.en: A negative prefix, an old verb of avoiding and an adjective ending make one compact word.
intro.cn: 一个否定前缀、一个古老的避开动词与一个形容词词尾，合成一个紧凑的词。

latinIntro.en: The root vitare, to avoid, also gives the rare English evasion and the everyday evade.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 vitare（避开）也产生了少见的 evasion 以及常用的 evade。

definition_zh: 不可避免地；必然地；难免
definition_en: in a way that cannot be avoided or prevented
core_image: 水坝出现裂缝，水只能一路往下冲
scene: 开会拖得太久，总会有人先走。Such long meetings inevitably end in silence and tired faces.
sceneCN: 这里 inevitably 是「不可避免地」（第 1 个义项：必然发生、无法阻止）；句意是这么长的会议必然以沉默和疲惫的面孔收场。

pos.zh: 副词：不可避免地；必然地；难免

forms.label: 无变化（副词无词形变化）

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词后缀 -ly，义为「不可避免的」
加名词后缀 -ity，义为「必然性」
去掉否定前缀，义为「可避免的」
同根动词，义为「逃避」

senses.title: In a way that cannot be stopped
senses.titleCN: 不可避免地：无法阻止地
senses.definition: in a way that cannot be prevented or escaped
senses.definitionCN: 以无法阻止或躲避的方式
senses.example: The old bridge will inevitably be replaced.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧桥不可避免地要被替换。
senses.why: The -ly ending turns the adjective into a comment on how something happens.
senses.whyCN: -ly 词尾把形容词变成对事情发生方式的评述。

senses.title: As a natural result
senses.definition: as the natural outcome of what came before
senses.definitionCN: 作为先前事情的必然结果
senses.example: Long hours of work inevitably lead to mistakes.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间工作必然导致错误。
senses.why: When cause and effect are tight, the adverb reports the result rather than a wish.
senses.whyCN: 因果紧密时，这个副词陈述的是结果，而不是愿望。

senses.title: Of course, as expected
senses.definition: as everyone expected, often with a mild sigh
senses.definitionCN: 如众人所料，常带一点叹息意味
senses.example: Inevitably, the bus was late again.
senses.exampleCN: 不出所料，公共汽车又晚了。
senses.why: The adverb can soften a complaint by presenting the event as nobody's fault.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词能把事件说成无人之过，从而缓和抱怨。

senses.title: In every case
senses.definition: in all cases, with no exception possible
senses.definitionCN: 在所有情况下，没有例外
senses.example: Such plans inevitably cost more than promised.
senses.exampleCN: 这类计划总是比承诺的花费更多。
senses.why: From one certain case the adverb generalizes to every case of the same kind.
senses.whyCN: 从一个确定的情形出发，副词推广到同类的一切情形。

intro.en: Inevitably is the adverb of inevitable, built with -ly on Latin in- plus evitare, to avoid.
intro.cn: inevitably 是 inevitable 的副词形式，由 -ly 加在拉丁 in- 与 evitare（避开）之上。

items.en: Evitare, to shun, came from ex plus vitare, to avoid.
items.cn: evitare（躲开）来自 ex 加 vitare（避开）。

items.en: The adjective evitabilis meant avoidable, and in- made it negative.
items.cn: 形容词 evitabilis 意为可避免的，加 in- 成为否定。

items.en: The word reached English through French as inevitable.
items.cn: 这个词经法语以 inevitable 的形式进入英语。

items.en: The adverb ending -ly was added, giving a word for how events must unfold.
items.cn: 加上副词词尾 -ly，得到描述事件必然展开方式的词。

items.en: Inevitably became common in argument and in everyday comment.
items.cn: inevitably 在论辩与日常评论中变得常用。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the inevitable family; the near-meaning group holds adverbs of certainty.
note.cn: 形近组收 inevitable 词族；近义组收表示必然的副词。

entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不可避免的」，是本词的原形。

entries.definition: The quality of being sure to happen.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「必然性」。
动词，义为「逃避」，与词根 evitare 同源。

entries.definition: As a logical or factual result.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「必然地」，偏逻辑推演。
副词，义为「确定地」，语气更肯定。

entries.definition: In a way that cannot be prevented.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「无法避免地」，是最直白的同义词。

normalIntro.en: The hooks strip the word down to in, evitare and -ly, then attach it to everyday predictions.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把词拆成 in、evitare 与 -ly，再与日常预判相连。

normal.en: Take inevitable and add -ly: the quality of the adjective becomes the manner of the verb.
normal.cn: 给 inevitable 加 -ly：形容词的性质变成动词的方式。

normal.en: In with the meaning not plus evitare, to avoid, gives the base sense of no escape.
normal.cn: 表示「不」的 in 加 evitare（避开），就是逃不掉的基本意思。

normal.en: The adverb usually sits before the verb, as in inevitably lead to.
normal.cn: 这个副词通常放在动词前，例如 inevitably lead to。

normal.en: Inevitably followed by a comma opens a sentence, like a shrug.
normal.cn: inevitably 加逗号放在句首，像一声无奈的耸肩。

normal.en: Almost inevitably is a common softener: the speaker allows one rare exception.
normal.cn: almost inevitably 是常见的缓和说法：说话人留了一个罕见的例外。

abstract.en: The adverb does not push; it merely removes the exits.
abstract.cn: 这个副词并不推人，它只是把出口一个个拿掉。

abstract.en: Inevitably is how hindsight speaks about tomorrow.
abstract.cn: inevitably 是后见之明谈论明天的方式。

abstract.en: Every -ly word tells you how to watch an event, and this one says watch it arrive.
abstract.cn: 每个 -ly 词都在告诉你如何看一件事，这个词说：看着它到来。

examples.en: The journey inevitably took longer than planned.
examples.cn: 这段行程不可避免地比计划更久。

examples.en: Inevitably, prices rose after the harvest failed.
examples.cn: 不出所料，歉收之后价格上涨了。

examples.en: Such changes inevitably affect the poorest families.
examples.cn: 这类变化必然影响最贫困的家庭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬喂它不来」——硬喂它也不来，事情照样必然发生。

root: inevitable（不可避免的）+ -ly（副词后缀）；词根为拉丁 evitare（避开）。

sensesIntro.en: From the bare idea of no escape, inevitably grows into natural result, expected routine and finally a sweeping every case.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「逃不掉」这一本义出发，inevitably 长出自然结果、预料之中的惯例，最后扩展到每个情形都如此。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water finding its only way down a cracked dam.
core.cn: 核心意象：水流从裂开的水坝上找到唯一的去路。

branches.en: CERTAINTY LINE: nothing can stop the event.
branches.cn: 确定线：没有什么能阻止这件事。

branches.en: CAUSE LINE: the result follows from what came before.
branches.cn: 因果线：结果由先前的事推出。

branches.en: ROUTINE LINE: the mild sigh of as expected.
branches.cn: 惯例线：一句「不出所料」的轻叹。

branches.en: SCOPE LINE: all cases, with no exception.
branches.cn: 范围线：所有情形，无一例外。

branches.en: COMMENT LINE: the speaker reports rather than blames.
branches.cn: 评述线：说话人只是陈述，而不是责怪。

intro.en: An adverb made by adding -ly to a negative Latin adjective.
intro.cn: 在否定式的拉丁形容词后加 -ly 构成的副词。

latinIntro.en: The avoiding root vitare also gives evade and evasion in everyday English.
latinIntro.cn: 表示避开的词根 vitare 还给了英语 evade 与 evasion。

definition_zh: 婴儿；幼儿；未成年人（法律用语）
definition_en: a very young child who cannot yet walk or talk, or a person below the legal age
core_image: 一个还不会说话的小婴儿，被人抱在怀里
scene: 病房里最安静的一张床躺着一个刚出生的孩子。The infant slept peacefully in her mother's arms.
sceneCN: 这里 infant 是「婴儿」（第 1 个义项：还不会走路说话的小宝宝）；句意是那个婴儿在母亲怀里安静地睡着。

pos.zh: 名词：婴儿；幼儿；未成年人
形容词：婴儿的；初期的

derivatives.zh: 由 infant 加名词后缀 -cy 构成，义为「婴儿期；初期」
由 infant 加表杀害的 -cide 构成，义为「杀婴」
加形容词后缀 -ile，义为「婴儿的；幼稚的」
同出拉丁 infans，义为「步兵」，原指年轻的随从

senses.title: A very young child
senses.definition: a baby or very young child who cannot yet speak
senses.definitionCN: 还不会说话的宝宝或很小的孩子
senses.example: The infant was wrapped in a soft blue blanket.
senses.exampleCN: 那个婴儿被裹在一条柔软的蓝毯子里。
senses.why: The Latin word means not speaking, and that is exactly what a baby cannot do.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词的意思是「不会说话」，而这正是宝宝做不到的事。

senses.title: A child below the legal age
senses.definition: in law, a person who has not yet reached adult age
senses.definitionCN: 法律上尚未成年的人
senses.example: The contract is not valid if signed by an infant.
senses.exampleCN: 如果是未成年人签署，这份合同无效。
senses.why: Since a minor cannot plead in court, the same word serves as a legal label.
senses.whyCN: 由于未成年人无法自己出庭，同一个词也就成了法律标签。

senses.title: Something in its early stage
senses.definition: a thing or system that is still new and undeveloped
senses.definitionCN: 还很新、尚未发展成熟的事物或体系
senses.example: The industry was still an infant in that decade.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个十年里，这个产业还处在婴儿期。
senses.why: A young thing cannot stand alone, so any new system borrows the picture.
senses.whyCN: 幼小的东西不能自立，于是任何新体系都借用了这个画面。

senses.title: Of a baby
senses.definition: relating to babies or to the care of babies
senses.definitionCN: 与婴儿或婴儿护理有关的
senses.example: Infant seats must be fitted in the back of the car.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿座椅必须装在汽车后座。
senses.why: The noun became an attribute: whatever belongs to the baby takes its name.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为定语：凡是属于婴儿的东西都用它来命名。

intro.en: Infant comes from Latin infans, literally not speaking, from in- plus fari, to speak.
intro.cn: infant 来自拉丁语 infans，字面意为「不会说话」，由 in- 与 fari（说话）构成。

items.en: Infans meant a young child, built on in-, not, plus fari, to speak.
items.cn: infans 指幼小的孩子，由 in-（不）加 fari（说话）构成。

items.en: The adjective was also used in law for a person too young to speak for himself.
items.cn: 这个形容词在法律上也指年幼到无法为自己发言的人。

items.en: Enfant carried the word into English in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 中古时期 enfant 把这个词带入英语。

items.en: The English form settled as infant, used for babies and for minors.
items.cn: 英语形式固定为 infant，用于婴儿与未成年人。

items.en: Infant broadened figuratively to mean anything still in its early stage.
items.cn: 近代以来 infant 比喻性地扩展为任何处于初期的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words from Latin fari and infans; the near-meaning group holds words for very young children.
note.cn: 形近组收出自拉丁 fari 与 infans 的词；近义组收指极幼小孩童的词。

entries.definition: The period of being a baby, or an early stage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「婴儿期；初期」，由 infant 加 -cy。

entries.definition: Typical of a baby, or childish.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「婴儿的；幼稚的」。
名词，义为「步兵」，同出拉丁 infans。
名词，义为「婴儿」，是最口语的说法。

entries.definition: A child who has just learned to walk.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蹒跚学步的孩子」，比 infant 稍大。

entries.definition: A person below the legal age.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「未成年人」，是法律上更常用的词。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the Latin sense of not speaking and the family of legal and medical words around it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借拉丁语「不会说话」的本义，以及围绕它的法律与医学词族。

normal.en: In- means not and fari means speak, so an infant is literally a not-speaking one.
normal.cn: in- 表示不，fari 表示说话，所以 infant 字面就是「不会说话的人」。

normal.en: Infancy covers both babyhood and the early stage of any project.
normal.cn: infancy 既指婴儿期，也指任何项目的初期。

normal.en: Infant school is an older British name for the first years of school.
normal.cn: infant school 是英国旧称，指最初几年的小学。

normal.en: In law an infant is a minor, so contracts with an infant need an adult.
normal.cn: 法律上 infant 就是未成年人，所以与他签约需要成年人。

normal.en: Infantile adds -ile and often carries the criticism of childish behavior.
normal.cn: infantile 加 -ile，常带有「幼稚」的批评意味。

abstract.en: Infant is a name built out of a silence: the one who cannot yet answer.
abstract.cn: infant 是从沉默里造出的名字：那个还不会回应的人。

abstract.en: Every beginning is an infant, whether a baby or a business.
abstract.cn: 一切开始都是 infant，无论是婴儿还是企业。

abstract.en: The word reminds us that speech is the line between infant and child.
abstract.cn: 这个词提醒我们：会说话是婴儿与儿童之间的界线。

examples.en: The infant was born on a cold winter night.
examples.cn: 这个婴儿出生在一个寒冷的冬夜。

examples.en: Infant health has improved greatly in this country.
examples.cn: 这个国家的婴儿健康水平已大幅提高。

examples.en: The scheme is still in its infant stage.
examples.cn: 这项计划仍处于初期阶段。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因粉他」——因为要给他冲奶粉，全家都围着这个小婴儿转。

root: 拉丁语 infans（不会说话的）= in-（不）+ fari（说话）；同族词有 infancy、infantile、infantry。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as the not-speaking one, then widens from baby to minor in law and, by picture, to anything still in its first stage.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词起初指「不会说话的人」，随后从婴儿扩展到法律上的未成年人，再借画面扩展到任何处于初期的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a baby held in arms, not yet able to speak.
core.cn: 核心意象：被抱在怀里、还不会说话的宝宝。

branches.en: BABY LINE: the small child who cannot yet speak.
branches.cn: 婴儿线：还不会说话的小孩。

branches.en: LAW LINE: dependence makes a person a minor.
branches.cn: 法律线：依赖他人使人成为未成年人。

branches.en: METAPHOR LINE: new systems borrow the baby picture.
branches.cn: 比喻线：新体系借用了婴儿的画面。

branches.en: ATTRIBUTE LINE: baby things take the name as a modifier.
branches.cn: 定语线：婴儿用品用它作修饰语。

branches.en: CARE LINE: everything given to babies is named infant something.
branches.cn: 护理线：给婴儿的一切东西都以 infant 命名。

intro.en: A Latin word of two parts, one denying speech, the other naming it.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁词，两部分一是否定说话，一是指称说话。

latinIntro.en: The root fari, to speak, also gives fable, fate and the legal phrase infant, all tied to speech.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 fari（说话）也产生了 fable、fate 以及法律用语 infant，都与言语相关。

definition_zh: 传染；感染；污染；影响（他人情绪）
definition_en: to pass a disease to a person, animal or plant, or to make something impure
core_image: 看不见的细菌从一个人手上跳到另一个人身上
scene: 医院里最怕伤口被弄脏。The wound became infected after the bandage fell off.
sceneCN: 这里 infect 是「使感染」（第 1 个义项：病菌进入体内）；句意是绷带掉了之后伤口被感染了。

pos.zh: 动词：传染；感染；污染；感染（情绪）

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -ion，义为「感染；传染」
加形容词后缀 -ious，义为「有传染性的」
加过去分词词尾，义为「受感染的」
加否定前缀 dis-，义为「给……消毒」

senses.title: To pass on a disease
senses.definition: to give a disease to a person, animal or plant
senses.definitionCN: 把疾病传给某人、动物或植物
senses.example: The virus can infect people through the air.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病毒可以通过空气传染给人。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to put in, and a germ put into a body is exactly an infection.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「放进去」，而病菌被放进身体就是感染。

senses.title: To make a wound impure
senses.definition: to let germs enter a cut so that it becomes diseased
senses.definitionCN: 让病菌进入伤口，使之发炎
senses.example: Wash your hands so you do not infect the cut.
senses.exampleCN: 洗手，免得让伤口感染。
senses.why: From an invisible thing put into the body, the word turns to the opening it enters.
senses.whyCN: 从被放进身体的无形之物，这个词转向它所进入的开口。

senses.title: To contaminate something
senses.definition: to make food, water or an object carry germs
senses.definitionCN: 使食物、水或物品带有病菌
senses.example: Raw meat can infect the tools used to cut it.
senses.exampleCN: 生肉会污染切它的工具。
senses.why: Anything that can carry a germ is said to be infected by it.
senses.whyCN: 凡是能携带病菌的东西，都可以说被它感染。

senses.title: To spread to computers
senses.definition: to put a harmful program into a computer or network
senses.definitionCN: 把有害程序放进电脑或网络
senses.example: A single email may infect a whole system.
senses.exampleCN: 一封邮件就可能让整个系统感染病毒。
senses.why: The medical sense is borrowed for computer viruses, which spread the same way.
senses.whyCN: 医学义被借给电脑病毒，因为二者的传播方式相同。

senses.title: To pass on a feeling
senses.definition: to make others share your mood, energy or idea
senses.definitionCN: 让别人分享你的情绪、活力或想法
senses.example: Her laughter infected the whole room.
senses.exampleCN: 她的笑声感染了整个房间。
senses.why: Emotion also spreads without contact, so the word carries cheerfulness as well as germs.
senses.whyCN: 情绪也无需接触就会传播，于是这个词既带病菌也带欢乐。

intro.en: Infect comes from Latin inficere, to put into or taint, built on in- plus facere, to make or do.
intro.cn: infect 来自拉丁语 inficere（放入、沾染），由 in- 加 facere（做、使）构成。

items.en: Inficere meant to dip in dye or taint something by putting another substance in it.
items.cn: inficere 意为浸入染料，或通过加入别的东西而污染。

items.en: The past participle infectus meant stained or corrupted.
items.cn: 过去分词 infectus 意为「被沾染的、腐坏的」。

items.en: The verb reached French and then Middle English with the sense of tainting.
items.cn: 这个动词经法语进入中古英语，带着「沾染」的意味。

items.en: As medicine advanced, infect narrowed towards germs entering the body.
items.cn: 随着医学进步，infect 收窄为病菌进入身体。

items.en: The word was later borrowed for computer viruses and for spreading feelings.
items.cn: 近代它又被借用于电脑病毒与情绪传播。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the Latin facere family; the near-meaning group holds words for passing on disease.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁 facere 词族；近义组收传播疾病的词。

entries.definition: A disease caused by germs, or their entry.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「感染；传染」。

entries.definition: Able to spread from person to person.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有传染性的」。
形容词，义为「完美的」，同出拉丁 facere。
动词，义为「污染」，强调混入有害物。

entries.definition: To pass on a disease to others.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「传播」，强调传递过程。
动词，义为「消毒」，与 infect 相反。

normalIntro.en: The hooks build on in- plus facere, then attach the word to wounds, offices and laughter.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子建立在 in- 加 facere 之上，再把词与伤口、办公室和笑声相连。

normal.en: In- means in and facere means make, so infect is to put something into something else.
normal.cn: in- 表示进入，facere 表示使，所以 infect 就是把某物放进另一物。

normal.en: Disinfect adds dis-, so it does the opposite: taking the germs out.
normal.cn: disinfect 加了 dis-，所以作用相反：把病菌拿走。

normal.en: Infection and infectious come from the same verb with -ion and -ious.
normal.cn: infection 与 infectious 由同一动词加 -ion 与 -ious 而来。

normal.en: Be infected with is the fixed frame for catching a disease.
normal.cn: be infected with 是表示「染上疾病」的固定框架。

normal.en: The computer sense keeps the medical picture: a virus that copies itself.
normal.cn: 电脑义保留了医学画面：一个会自我复制的病毒。

abstract.en: Infection is invisible entry: nothing is seen, but everything is changed.
abstract.cn: 感染是无形的进入：什么都看不见，一切却都变了。

abstract.en: A mood can infect a room exactly as a germ infects a body.
abstract.cn: 情绪能感染一间屋子，正如病菌能感染一具身体。

abstract.en: The word is about putting in, and the harm comes from what got in.
abstract.cn: 这个词讲的是放进去，而伤害来自进去的东西。

examples.en: The doctor said the cut would infect if left open.
examples.cn: 医生说这个伤口敞着会长染。

examples.en: Two hundred people were infected with the virus.
examples.cn: 有两百人感染了这种病毒。

examples.en: The software can infect every computer on the network.
examples.cn: 这个软件能感染网络上的每一台电脑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬费克特」——硬要费心克服的特种病菌，会不断传染。

root: 拉丁语 inficere（放入、沾染）= in-（进入）+ facere（做、使）；同族词有 infection、infectious、perfect。

sensesIntro.en: From the physical act of putting a taint into something, infect narrows to germs in a body, widens to contaminated objects, and is borrowed again for computer viruses and for feelings.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把污物放进某物的具体动作出发，infect 收窄为身体里的病菌，扩展到被污染的物件，再被借用于电脑病毒与情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an invisible germ passing from one hand to another.
core.cn: 核心意象：看不见的病菌从一只手跳到另一只手。

branches.en: DISEASE LINE: the germ enters a living body.
branches.cn: 疾病线：病菌进入活体。

branches.en: WOUND LINE: the entry point becomes diseased.
branches.cn: 伤口线：入口处发炎病变。

branches.en: OBJECT LINE: food, water and tools carry germs.
branches.cn: 物件线：食物、水和工具携带病菌。

branches.en: MACHINE LINE: a virus enters a computer.
branches.cn: 机器线：病毒进入电脑。

branches.en: FEELING LINE: a mood spreads like an infection.
branches.cn: 情感线：情绪像感染一样传播。

intro.en: A Latin verb of putting in, whose family covers medicine, cleaning and computer security.
intro.cn: 一个表示「放入」的拉丁动词，其词族覆盖医学、清洁与电脑安全。

latinIntro.en: The root facere, to make, appears everywhere in English, from factory to effect and perfect.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 facere（做、使）遍布英语，从 factory 到 effect 与 perfect。

definition_zh: 感染；传染；传染病
definition_en: a disease caused by germs entering the body, or the process of this happening
core_image: 伤口周围红起来，热得发烫
scene: 换药时护士反复看伤口边缘。There is a slight infection around the stitches.
sceneCN: 这里 infection 是「感染」（第 1 个义项：病菌进入身体引起的病变）；句意是缝线周围有轻微的感染。

pos.zh: 名词：感染；传染；传染病

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀 -ion，义为「传染；感染」
加 -ious 构成，义为「有传染性的」
加 -ed 构成，义为「受感染的」
加 dis- 与 -ion，义为「消毒」

senses.title: A disease from germs
senses.definition: an illness caused by bacteria or viruses entering the body
senses.definitionCN: 细菌或病毒进入身体所引起的疾病
senses.example: The infection spread from his throat to his lungs.
senses.exampleCN: 感染从他的喉咙蔓延到肺部。
senses.why: The noun names the state that infect produces: something harmful has been put in.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名 infect 所造成状态：有害之物被放了进来。

senses.title: The process of catching disease
senses.definition: the process by which germs enter and multiply in the body
senses.definitionCN: 病菌进入身体并繁殖的过程
senses.example: Doctors watched for signs of infection after the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 手术后医生密切观察感染的迹象。
senses.why: -ion turns the verb into the whole process, not only its result.
senses.whyCN: -ion 把这个动词变成整个过程，而不只是结果。

senses.title: A wound that turns bad
senses.definition: a cut or wound that has become painful, hot and red from germs
senses.definitionCN: 伤口因病菌而变得疼痛、发热、发红
senses.example: Clean the cut to prevent infection.
senses.exampleCN: 清洗伤口以防感染。
senses.why: The word focuses on the opening where germs first got in.
senses.whyCN: 这个词聚焦于病菌最初进入的那个开口。

senses.title: A disease passing to others
senses.definition: a disease that can be passed from person to person
senses.definitionCN: 能在人与人之间传递的疾病
senses.example: The clinic treats hundreds of infections each winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所每年冬天治疗数百例传染病。
senses.why: Countable and plural, the noun names particular diseases rather than the state.
senses.whyCN: 可数且用复数时，这个名词指具体的疾病而不是状态。

senses.title: Bad influence spreading
senses.definition: the spread of a harmful idea or habit from person to person
senses.definitionCN: 有害想法或习惯在人与人之间扩散
senses.example: The police spoke of an infection of fear in the town.
senses.exampleCN: 警方谈到恐惧在这座小镇里蔓延。
senses.why: Anything that spreads like a germ borrows the same noun.
senses.whyCN: 凡是像病菌一样扩散的东西都借用了这个名词。

intro.en: Infection is the noun of infect, from Latin inficere, to put into or taint, on in- plus facere, to make.
intro.cn: infection 是 infect 的名词形式，出自拉丁语 inficere（放入、沾染），由 in- 加 facere 构成。

items.en: Infectio meant a dipping in, and later a contamination or corruption.
items.cn: infectio 意为浸染，后指污染、腐坏。

items.en: The verb inficere had a strong sense of tainting something with a dye.
items.cn: 动词 inficere 强烈含有以染料沾染某物之义。

items.en: The word travelled into French with the meaning of contamination.
items.cn: 这个词带着污染之义进入法语。

items.en: Medical writers fixed infection as the entry and growth of germs in the body.
items.cn: 医学作者把 infection 固定为病菌进入身体并繁殖。

items.en: The countable plural infections came to mean particular diseases.
items.cn: 可数复数 infections 逐渐指具体疾病。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the -fect family; the near-meaning group holds words for disease and its spread.
note.cn: 形近组收 -fect 词族；近义组收疾病及其传播的词。

entries.definition: To pass germs into a body.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「传染；感染」，是本词的原形。

entries.definition: Able to be passed between people.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有传染性的」。

entries.definition: A result produced by a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「效果」，与 infect 同为 facere 词族。
名词，义为「疾病」，比 infection 更宽泛。

entries.definition: The spreading of disease by contact.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「接触传染」，强调接触方式。

entries.definition: Redness and swelling of body tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「发炎」，常伴随感染但不等于感染。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the -ion ending, the partner adjective, and the everyday talk about wounds.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 -ion 词尾、配套形容词以及关于伤口的日常说法。

normal.en: Add -ion to infect and you have the state or the process it produces.
normal.cn: 给 infect 加上 -ion，就得到它造成的状态或过程。

normal.en: Infect is the verb, infectious is the adjective, infection is the noun.
normal.cn: infect 是动词，infectious 是形容词，infection 是名词。

normal.en: Risk of infection is the phrase used in hospitals and on medicine boxes.
normal.cn: risk of infection 是医院与药品包装上常见的说法。

normal.en: Ear infection and chest infection name the place where germs settled.
normal.cn: ear infection 与 chest infection 指明病菌落脚之处。

normal.en: Disinfection adds dis-: the -ion noun of taking the germs out.
normal.cn: disinfection 加了 dis-：表示把病菌去掉的 -ion 名词。

abstract.en: Infection is a story told by the body: heat, redness, swelling.
abstract.cn: 感染是身体讲的一个故事：发热、发红、肿胀。

abstract.en: Unseen things that enter are the quietest kind of invasion.
abstract.cn: 进入体内的无形之物，是最安静的入侵。

abstract.en: Every infection is a reminder that the border of a body is soft.
abstract.cn: 每一次感染都提醒我们，身体的边界是软的。

examples.en: The infection was cured with a simple course of pills.
examples.cn: 这次感染用一个简单疗程的药片就治好了。

examples.en: Doctors try to reduce the risk of infection during surgery.
examples.cn: 医生努力降低手术期间的感染风险。

examples.en: A small infection in the finger can spread quickly.
examples.cn: 手指上一处小小的感染也可能迅速扩散。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因费克生」——因为费力克服，才把这感染生出的病治好。

root: infect（感染）+ -ion（名词后缀）；infect 出自拉丁语 inficere（放入、沾染）。

sensesIntro.en: Infection moves from the general state of being tainted, to the germ disease, to the process, to a single inflamed wound, and finally to any spreading harm.
sensesIntro.cn: infection 从被沾染的一般状态，走向病菌引起的疾病、传染的过程、单处发炎的伤口，最后扩展到任何一种扩散的伤害。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: red hot skin around a small cut.
core.cn: 核心意象：小伤口周围红热发烫的皮肤。

branches.en: DISEASE LINE: germs settle and cause illness.
branches.cn: 疾病线：病菌落脚并致病。

branches.en: PROCESS LINE: entry and growth over time.
branches.cn: 过程线：进入与繁殖的时间过程。

branches.en: WOUND LINE: one spot turns red and hot.
branches.cn: 伤口线：某一处变得红热。

branches.en: DISEASE COUNT: the plural names particular illnesses.
branches.cn: 病例线：复数指具体疾病。

branches.en: METAPHOR LINE: any harm that passes person to person.
branches.cn: 比喻线：任何在人与人之间传递的伤害。

intro.en: A noun in -ion whose family spreads from medicine into cleaning and machinery.
intro.cn: 一个以 -ion 结尾的名词，词族从医学延伸到清洁与机器领域。

latinIntro.en: The root facere, to make, gives infection, effect, defect and many other English words.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 facere（做）产生了 infection、effect、defect 等众多英语词。

definition_zh: 传染的；有传染性的；有感染力的
definition_en: able to pass from one person to another, or able to make others feel the same
core_image: 一个人打一个喷嚏，旁边的人纷纷后退
scene: 孩子发烧不能去学校。Measles is highly infectious, so she must stay home.
sceneCN: 这里 infectious 是「有传染性的」（第 1 个义项：疾病能传给别人）；句意是麻疹传染性很强，所以她必须待在家里。

pos.zh: 形容词：传染的；有传染性的；有感染力的

derivatives.zh: 名词形式，义为「感染」
动词原形，义为「传染」
加 -ly，义为「有感染力地」
加 -ness，义为「传染性；感染力」

senses.title: Able to spread disease
senses.definition: able to pass a disease from one living thing to another
senses.definitionCN: 能把疾病从一个生物传给另一个
senses.example: The flu is most infectious in the first few days.
senses.exampleCN: 流感在最初几天传染性最强。
senses.why: The -ious ending means full of, here full of the power to infect.
senses.whyCN: -ious 词尾意为「充满」，此处即充满传染的力量。

senses.title: Able to be contacted by germs
senses.definition: carrying germs that can pass to others, said of a person
senses.definitionCN: 指某人身带可传给别人的病菌
senses.example: She is still infectious and should not visit the baby.
senses.exampleCN: 她仍然带菌具有传染性，不该去看宝宝。
senses.why: The quality can sit in the person rather than in the disease.
senses.whyCN: 这种性质可以落在人身上，而不只落在疾病上。

senses.title: Spreading cheer, not germs
senses.definition: spreading a feeling or quality quickly to others
senses.definitionCN: 把某种情绪或品质迅速传给别人
senses.example: His infectious good humour lifted the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他那有感染力的好心情带动了整个会议。
senses.why: The same spreading power is borrowed for moods, laughter and enthusiasm.
senses.whyCN: 同样的扩散力被借用于情绪、笑声与热情。

senses.title: Passing from mind to mind
senses.definition: spreading quickly among people, as of an idea or fear
senses.definitionCN: 指想法或恐惧在人群中快速传开
senses.example: The rumour was infectious and soon everyone believed it.
senses.exampleCN: 这则传言极具传染性，很快人人都信了。
senses.why: The adjective stretches further still, to ideas that spread without contact.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词还能进一步延伸到无需接触就传开的思想。

intro.en: Infectious adds Latin -iosus, full of, to infectus, the participle of inficere, to taint.
intro.cn: infectious 把拉丁 -iosus（充满）加到 infectus 上，后者是 inficere（沾染）的分词。

items.en: Inficere meant to put in or taint, with facere, to make, as its second part.
items.cn: inficere 意为放入或沾染，后半部分为 facere（做）。

items.en: The adjective infectiosus described air, water or a person full of contagion.
items.cn: 形容词 infectiosus 描述充满病源的空气、水或人。

items.en: The form reached French and then English, keeping the medical sense.
items.cn: 该形式经法语进入英语，保留医学含义。

items.en: Infectious was early applied to the plague and to fevers.
items.cn: infectious 早期用于瘟疫与热病。

items.en: The figurative use for laughter and enthusiasm appeared in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 用于笑声与热情的比喻义在十九世纪出现。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the infection family; the near-meaning group holds adjectives of spreading.
note.cn: 形近组收 infection 词族；近义组收描述传播的形容词。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「感染」，是本词的名词形式。
动词，义为「传染」。
形容词，义为「珍贵的」，只是拼写相近，词源不同。
形容词，义为「接触传染的」，强调接触。
形容词，口语中义为「易传染的」。
形容词，义为「病毒式的」，常指网络传播。

normalIntro.en: The hooks join the -ious ending to the family, then follow the word from illness to laughter.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 -ious 词尾同词族相连，再随词义从疾病走到笑声。

normal.en: The -ious ending means full of, so infectious means full of the power to infect.
normal.cn: -ious 意为充满，所以 infectious 就是充满传染的力量。

normal.en: Contagious stresses touch, infectious stresses germs, and often both are used loosely.
normal.cn: contagious 强调接触，infectious 强调病菌，日常常混用。

normal.en: Infectious laughter is the phrase that shows the figurative side.
normal.cn: infectious laughter 展示了这个词的比喻一面。

normal.en: A person and a disease can both be described as infectious.
normal.cn: 人和疾病都可以用 infectious 来形容。

normal.en: Drop -ious and add -ion to get the noun infection.
normal.cn: 去掉 -ious 加 -ion 就得到名词 infection。

abstract.en: Infectious measures how far something can travel without moving itself.
abstract.cn: infectious 衡量的是某物不动却能把影响传多远。

abstract.en: Besides illness, an infectious person gives away their mood.
abstract.cn: 除了疾病，有感染力的人还会把心情分给别人。

abstract.en: The -ious suffix always suggests abundance: full of a force that seeks the next person.
abstract.cn: -ious 词尾总暗示丰盈：充满一种要寻找下一个人的力量。

examples.en: Chickenpox is infectious before the spots appear.
examples.cn: 水痘在出疹子之前就具有传染性。

examples.en: Her infectious laugh made everyone relax.
examples.cn: 她那富有感染力的笑声让所有人都放松下来。

examples.en: The doctor ordered him to stay at home while he was infectious.
examples.cn: 医生嘱咐他在具传染性期间待在家里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阴飞克死」——阴冷的病毒乱飞，把体弱的人克死，传染性极强。

root: 拉丁语 infectiosus = infectus（被沾染的）+ -iosus（充满）；词根为 inficere（放入、沾染）。

sensesIntro.en: Infectious begins as full of contagion, moves to the person who carries it, and then to moods and ideas that spread equally fast.
sensesIntro.cn: infectious 起初指充满病源，随后转指携带病源的人，再转向同样传播极快的情绪与想法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sneeze that makes the whole room step back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个喷嚏让整个房间的人后退。

branches.en: DISEASE LINE: an illness able to pass on.
branches.cn: 疾病线：能传下去的疾病。

branches.en: PERSON LINE: a person still carrying germs.
branches.cn: 人体线：仍然带菌的人。

branches.en: MOOD LINE: laughter and cheer spread without germs.
branches.cn: 情绪线：笑声与欢乐无需病菌也会传播。

branches.en: IDEA LINE: rumours pass like a fever.
branches.cn: 观念线：传言像发热一样传播。

branches.en: SPREAD LINE: one force of passing things on.
branches.cn: 传播线：同一种把东西传出去的力量。

intro.en: An adjective in -ious built on the infection family, used for germs and for feelings alike.
intro.cn: 一个以 -ious 结尾、建立在 infection 词族上的形容词，既用于病菌也用于情绪。

latinIntro.en: The suffix -iosus was the Latin way of saying full of, and English kept it in countless words.
latinIntro.cn: 后缀 -iosus 是拉丁语表达「充满」的方式，英语在无数词里保留了它。

definition_zh: 推断；推知；推论
definition_en: to reach an opinion or conclusion from evidence rather than from direct statement
core_image: 几块拼图凑在一起，缺的那一角自动显现
scene: 侦探看着地上一串湿脚印。From the wet footprints we can infer that someone came in during the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 infer 是「推断」（第 1 个义项：根据证据推出结论）；句意是我们能从湿脚印推断出有人在下雨时进来过。

pos.zh: 动词：推断；推知；推论
及物：由……推断出

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -ence，义为「推断；推论」
加 -ial，义为「推论的」
加 -able，义为「可推断的」
同出拉丁 ferre，义为「商议；授予」，前缀不同

senses.title: To work out a conclusion
senses.definition: to form a conclusion using the facts you have
senses.definitionCN: 利用已有的事实得出一个结论
senses.example: From the empty cup we inferred that he had already left.
senses.exampleCN: 从那个空杯子我们推断他已经走了。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to bring in, and a conclusion is something you bring in from clues.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「带进来」，而结论就是从线索里带进来的东西。

senses.title: To read meaning into words
senses.definition: to understand something that is suggested but not said
senses.definitionCN: 理解被暗示而非明说的内容
senses.example: I infer from your silence that you disagree.
senses.exampleCN: 从你的沉默里我揣摩出你并不同意。
senses.why: What is not spoken still carries meaning, and the reader must carry it out.
senses.whyCN: 没有说出口的话也带含义，听话的人要把它带出来。

senses.title: To deduce in logic
senses.definition: to move from premises to a necessary conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 从前提出发推出必然的结论
senses.example: From these two rules we can infer the third.
senses.exampleCN: 由这两条规则我们可以推出第三条。
senses.why: In strict logic the word is the technical name for derivation.
senses.whyCN: 在严格逻辑中，这个词是「推导」的专业名称。

senses.title: To guess indirectly
senses.definition: to make an educated guess rather than a certain judgement
senses.definitionCN: 作有依据的猜测，而非确定的判断
senses.example: We can only infer what she meant by that note.
senses.exampleCN: 我们只能猜她想用那张便条表达什么。
senses.why: Because evidence is often incomplete, the verb also covers careful guessing.
senses.whyCN: 由于证据常常不全，这个动词也包含谨慎的猜测。

intro.en: Infer comes from Latin inferre, to bring in, from in- plus ferre, to carry.
intro.cn: infer 来自拉丁语 inferre（带进来），由 in- 加 ferre（携带）构成。

items.en: Inferre meant to bring in or bring upon, built on in- plus ferre, to carry.
items.cn: inferre 意为带入或招致，由 in- 加 ferre（携带）构成。

items.en: In logic it meant to bring a conclusion into an argument.
items.cn: 在逻辑中它指把一个结论带入论证。

items.en: The verb passed into French and then into English in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 这个动词经法语于十六世纪进入英语。

items.en: Infer was long used for both drawing and offering a conclusion.
items.cn: infer 长期兼指推出结论与提出结论。

items.en: Modern usage keeps infer for the listener and imply for the speaker.
items.cn: 现代用法中 infer 归听者，imply 归说者。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the ferre family; the near-meaning group holds verbs of reasoning.
note.cn: 形近组收 ferre 词族；近义组收推理类动词。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「推断」，是本词的名词形式。
动词，义为「商议；授予」，同出 ferre。

entries.definition: To carry from one place to another.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「转移」，同出 ferre。

entries.definition: To reach a conclusion by logic.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「演绎；推断」，偏逻辑推演。
动词，义为「断定」，是推断的结果动作。
动词，义为「暗示」，动作来自说者而非听者。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use ferre, to carry, the doubled r in the endings and the split from imply.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 ferre（携带）、词尾双写 r 以及与 imply 的分工。

normal.en: Ferre means carry, so to infer is to carry a conclusion in from the evidence.
normal.cn: ferre 意为携带，所以 infer 就是从证据里把结论带进来。

normal.en: The past form doubles the r: inferred and inferring.
normal.cn: 过去形式双写 r：inferred 与 inferring。

normal.en: Inference is the noun, and inferential is the adjective of logic.
normal.cn: inference 是名词，inferential 是逻辑意义上的形容词。

normal.en: Infer from is the standard pattern: infer X from Y.
normal.cn: infer from 是标准模式：由 Y 推断出 X。

normal.en: The listener infers, the speaker implies: the arrow points opposite ways.
normal.cn: 听者 infer，说者 imply：箭头方向正好相反。

abstract.en: Inference is the shadow a fact casts into the mind.
abstract.cn: 推断是一个事实投进心里的影子。

abstract.en: To infer is to trust the gap: the missing piece is filled by reason, not by seeing.
abstract.cn: 推断是信任那道缝隙：缺的一块由推理补上，而不是由眼睛看到。

abstract.en: The word carries something in, and what it carries is a small act of belief.
abstract.cn: 这个词是把某种东西带进来，而带进来的是一个微小的信念行为。

examples.en: We can infer from his tone that he is angry.
examples.cn: 从他的语气我们可以推断他生气了。

examples.en: Nothing can be inferred from a single case.
examples.cn: 单凭一个案例什么都推断不出来。

examples.en: Readers are left to infer the ending for themselves.
examples.cn: 读者要自己推断出结局。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因佛」——因为拜佛求签，人要自己推断签上的意思。

root: 拉丁语 inferre（带入）= in-（进入）+ ferre（携带）；同族词有 inference、confer、transfer。

sensesIntro.en: From carrying a conclusion in, infer covers reading unspoken meaning, formal logical derivation and cautious guessing when evidence is thin.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「把结论带进来」出发，infer 涵盖揣摩言外之意、形式逻辑的推导，以及证据不足时的谨慎猜测。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the last piece sliding into a jigsaw puzzle.
core.cn: 核心意象：最后一块拼图滑入缺口。

branches.en: CLUE LINE: facts lead to a conclusion.
branches.cn: 线索线：事实导向结论。

branches.en: SILENCE LINE: unspoken meaning is read out.
branches.cn: 沉默线：言外之意被读出来。

branches.en: LOGIC LINE: premises yield a necessary result.
branches.cn: 逻辑线：前提推出必然结果。

branches.en: GUESS LINE: the evidence is not enough.
branches.cn: 猜测线：证据并不充分。

branches.en: MOVEMENT LINE: something is carried in from outside.
branches.cn: 移动线：有东西从外面被带进来。

intro.en: A Latin verb of carrying, which builds a large family of English words with different prefixes.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语「携带」动词，用不同前缀造出了大量英语词。

latinIntro.en: The root ferre, to carry, appears in transfer, refer, offer and many other words.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 ferre（携带）出现在 transfer、refer、offer 等大量词中。

definition_zh: 推断；推论；结论
definition_en: a conclusion reached from evidence, or the act of reaching it
core_image: 桌上一张空椅子、一杯冷茶，人走了
scene: 房间里灯还亮着，人却不见了。Her silence was an inference that the answer was no.
sceneCN: 这里 inference 是「推断出的结论」（第 1 个义项：由证据得出的判断）；句意是她的沉默让人推断答案是「不」。

pos.zh: 名词：推断；推论；结论；推理过程

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ence，义为「推断」
加 -ial，义为「推论的」
加 -able，义为「可推断的」
加 -ly，义为「通过推论」

senses.title: A conclusion from evidence
senses.definition: a judgement you form because of clues rather than on direct information
senses.definitionCN: 因线索而形成的判断，而非依据直接信息
senses.example: The police drew a simple inference from the wet shoes.
senses.exampleCN: 警方从那双湿鞋作出一个简单的推断。
senses.why: The noun names what the verb produces, a conclusion carried in from evidence.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名动词所产出的东西：从证据里带进来的结论。

senses.title: The act of reasoning
senses.definition: the mental act of moving from evidence to a conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 从证据走向结论的心理活动
senses.example: Inference is slower than seeing and often more careful.
senses.exampleCN: 推论比看见慢，也常常更谨慎。
senses.why: -ence can name either the result or the activity, and here it names both.
senses.whyCN: -ence 既能指结果也能指活动，这里两者兼有。

senses.title: A method in science
senses.definition: a formal procedure for reaching conclusions in logic or statistics
senses.definitionCN: 在逻辑或统计中得出正式结论的方法
senses.example: Statistical inference allows us to judge a whole population from a sample.
senses.exampleCN: 统计推断让我们从样本判断总体。
senses.why: When rules are fixed, the activity becomes a named method.
senses.whyCN: 当规则固定下来，这种活动就成为一个有名目的方法。

senses.title: Something read between the lines
senses.definition: a meaning understood but not stated
senses.definitionCN: 被理解却未被明说的含义
senses.example: The inference from her letter was clear: she would not come.
senses.exampleCN: 她信中隐含的意思很清楚：她不会来。
senses.why: Unspoken meaning has to be built by the reader, so it too is an inference.
senses.whyCN: 未说出的含义要由读者建构，因此它也是 infer 的结果。

senses.title: A guess, if weak
senses.definition: an uncertain conclusion reached with too little evidence
senses.definitionCN: 证据不足时得出的不确定结论
senses.example: That was an inference, not a fact.
senses.exampleCN: 那只是推断，并不是事实。
senses.why: The noun reminds us that a conclusion without proof still carries risk.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词提醒我们：没有证据的结论仍有风险。

intro.en: Inference is the English noun of infer, from Latin inferre, to bring in, as in a conclusion into an argument.
intro.cn: inference 是 infer 的英语名词形式，出自拉丁语 inferre（带入），如同把结论带入论证。

items.en: Inferre meant to bring in, on in- plus ferre, to carry.
items.cn: inferre 意为带入，由 in- 加 ferre（携带）构成。

items.en: In grammar and logic, inferre could name the idea that follows from words.
items.cn: 在语法与逻辑中，inferre 可指由词句推出的想法。

items.en: The noun reached French before English took it in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 这个名词先进入法语，十六世纪再由英语吸收。

items.en: Inference became the standard word in logic for a step from premises.
items.cn: inference 成为逻辑中表示「从前提出发的一步」的标准词。

items.en: The plural inferences covers everyday guesses as well as formal proofs.
items.cn: 复数 inferences 既指日常猜测，也指正式证明。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the infer family; the near-meaning group holds words for conclusions.
note.cn: 形近组收 infer 词族；近义组收表示结论的词。

entries.definition: To reach a conclusion from evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「推断」，是本词的原形。
形容词，义为「推论的」。

entries.definition: The act of getting in the way.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「干扰」，只是拼写相近，词源不同。
名词，义为「演绎；推论」，偏逻辑推导。
名词，义为「结论」，是最通用的说法。
名词，义为「猜测」，证据更少。

normalIntro.en: The hooks tie the noun to its verb, its adjective and the set phrases used in exams and science.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把名词与动词、形容词以及考试和科学中的固定说法连起来。

normal.en: Infer is the verb and inference is the noun: draw an inference.
normal.cn: infer 是动词，inference 是名词：draw an inference。

normal.en: The -ence ending marks a state or act, as in difference and patience.
normal.cn: -ence 词尾标示状态或行为，如 difference、patience。

normal.en: By inference means not by direct statement but by reasoning.
normal.cn: by inference 意为不是听来的，而是推出来的。

normal.en: Statistical inference is the formal version, judging a population from a sample.
normal.cn: statistical inference 是正式用法：从样本判断总体。

normal.en: Inferential swaps -ence for -ial and becomes the adjective of logic.
normal.cn: inferential 把 -ence 换成 -ial，成为逻辑意义上的形容词。

abstract.en: An inference is a bridge no one built for you; you build it from the clues.
abstract.cn: 推断是一座没人替你搭的桥，你从线索里自己搭。

abstract.en: The word means carried in: what the mind carries from the world to itself.
abstract.cn: 这个词意为「带进来」：心灵从世界带向自身的东西。

abstract.en: Every inference is a small promise that the world is consistent.
abstract.cn: 每一个推断都是一个小承诺：世界是前后一致的。

examples.en: The report draws a clear inference about the cause of the fire.
examples.cn: 报告对火灾原因作出了明确的推断。

examples.en: We should not base an inference on so little evidence.
examples.cn: 我们不该凭这么少的证据下推断。

examples.en: Her inference was correct: the letter never arrived.
examples.cn: 她的推断是对的：那封信从未寄到。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因佛认死」——因为拜了佛就认定死理，全凭推断。

root: infer（推断）+ -ence（名词后缀）；词根为拉丁 ferre（携带）。

sensesIntro.en: Inference can mean the conclusion, the act of concluding, the formal method, the meaning read between lines, or a weak guess.
sensesIntro.cn: inference 既可指结论本身，也可指得出结论的动作、正式的方法、读出的言外之意，或证据不足的猜测。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cold cup of tea and an empty chair.
core.cn: 核心意象：一杯冷茶和一张空椅子。

branches.en: RESULT LINE: the conclusion itself.
branches.cn: 结果线：结论本身。

branches.en: ACT LINE: the mental step from clue to answer.
branches.cn: 动作线：从线索到答案的心理一步。

branches.en: METHOD LINE: fixed rules in logic and statistics.
branches.cn: 方法线：逻辑与统计中的固定规则。

branches.en: IMPLICIT LINE: meaning read from what was not said.
branches.cn: 隐含线：从没说出口的话里读出含义。

branches.en: RISK LINE: a conclusion may still be wrong.
branches.cn: 风险线：结论仍可能是错的。

intro.en: A noun ending in -ence built on the Latin verb of carrying.
intro.cn: 一个以 -ence 结尾、建立在拉丁「携带」动词上的名词。

latinIntro.en: The root ferre, to carry, also gives conference, reference and interference.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 ferre（携带）也产生了 conference、reference 与 interference。

definition_zh: 较差的；下级的；下方的；下属
definition_en: lower in quality, rank or position than someone or something else
core_image: 同一座楼里，楼下的办公室比楼上简陋
scene: 公司里同一张表，上下两栏对比鲜明。The cheaper model is clearly inferior to the one above it.
sceneCN: 这里 inferior 是「较差的」（第 1 个义项：质量上不如别的）；句意是那个便宜的型号明显不如它上面那款。

pos.zh: 形容词：较差的；下级的；下方的
名词：下级；下属

derivatives.zh: 加 -ity，义为「低劣；自卑」
反义同源词，义为「较好的；上级的」
加 -ly，义为「较低地」
固定短语，义为「自卑情结」

senses.title: Lower in quality
senses.definition: not as good as something else of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 在同类之中不如别的
senses.example: The copy is inferior to the original in every way.
senses.exampleCN: 这份副本在各方面都不如原件。
senses.why: The Latin comparative means lower, and lower quality is the everyday extension of lower place.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁比较级意为「更低的」，而质量更低就是位置更低的日常延伸。

senses.title: Lower in rank
senses.definition: having a less important position in a group
senses.definitionCN: 在群体中处于较不重要的位置
senses.example: He was careful how he spoke to inferior officers.
senses.exampleCN: 他对下级军官说话很谨慎。
senses.why: Rank is imagined as height, so those below are called inferior.
senses.whyCN: 等级被想象成高度，位于下面的人就被称为 inferior。

senses.title: Physically below
senses.definition: situated lower, as in anatomy
senses.definitionCN: 位置较低，常用于解剖学
senses.example: The inferior vena cava carries blood upward to the heart.
senses.exampleCN: 下腔静脉把血液向上输送回心脏。
senses.why: In anatomy the word keeps its literal Latin sense of below.
senses.whyCN: 在解剖学里，这个词保留了拉丁语「在下面」的本义。

senses.title: A person of lower rank
senses.definition: a person who ranks below another at work
senses.definitionCN: 在工作中级别低于他人的人
senses.example: She treats her inferiors with respect.
senses.exampleCN: 她尊重自己的下属。
senses.why: The adjective used as a noun names the people who rank lower.
senses.whyCN: 形容词作名词，指级别较低的人。

senses.title: Feeling less worthy
senses.definition: feeling that you are worse than others
senses.definitionCN: 觉得自己不如别人
senses.example: Years of comparison left him feeling inferior.
senses.exampleCN: 常年的比较让他感到自卑。
senses.why: A social rank turns inward and becomes a private mood.
senses.whyCN: 社会等级转向内心，就成为私人的情绪。

intro.en: Inferior is the Latin comparative of inferus, below, literally more below, like the lower one of two.
intro.cn: inferior 是拉丁语 inferus（下面的）的比较级，字面即「更靠下的」，如同两者中较低的那个。

items.en: Inferus meant low or below, and its comparative was inferior, lower.
items.cn: inferus 意为低或在下，其比较级为 inferior（更低的）。

items.en: The same family gave infernus, of the underworld, and the English infernal.
items.cn: 同族词还产生了 infernus（冥界的）以及英语 infernal。

items.en: The comparative form came into English through French in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 这个比较级形式在中古时期经法语进入英语。

items.en: Inferior first described place, then rank, then quality.
items.cn: inferior 先描述位置，再描述等级，最后描述质量。

items.en: The phrase inferior to replaced older patterns of comparison.
items.cn: 短语 inferior to 取代了更早的比较说法。

note.en: The look-alike group holds Latin comparatives; the near-meaning group holds words describing lesser quality or rank.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁比较级词；近义组收描述较差质量或较低等级的词。

entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「较好的；上级的」，与 inferior 相对。
名词，义为「低劣；自卑」。
名词，义为「烈火；地狱」，同出拉丁 infernus。
形容词，义为「更差的」，最日常的说法。
形容词或名词，义为「下级的；下级」，用于组织。
形容词，义为「二流的」，强调质量平庸。

normalIntro.en: The hooks build on the Latin comparative -ior and the fixed pair inferior to, with superior as its mirror.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子建立在拉丁比较级 -ior 与固定搭配 inferior to 上，并以 superior 作镜面。

normal.en: The -ior ending marks a Latin comparative, as in superior and senior.
normal.cn: -ior 词尾标示拉丁比较级，如 superior、senior。

normal.en: Inferior always takes to: inferior to this one, never than.
normal.cn: inferior 总是接 to：inferior to this one，而不用 than。

normal.en: Superior is its exact mirror, built on super, above.
normal.cn: superior 是它精确的镜面，建立在 super（在上）之上。

normal.en: Inferiority complex is the psychological phrase for feeling less than others.
normal.cn: inferiority complex 是表示自卑心理的固定搭配。

normal.en: In anatomy the word simply means below, with no judgement at all.
normal.cn: 在解剖学里这个词只表示「在下面」，毫无贬义。

abstract.en: Inferior is altitude turned into judgement: what is low is thought less.
abstract.cn: inferior 是把高度变成了判断：低的就被认为差。

abstract.en: The word compares, it never measures alone; something is always above it.
abstract.cn: 这个词只在比较中存在，它从不单独出现：总有什么在上面。

abstract.en: To feel inferior is to keep a ladder in the mind and stand on a low step.
abstract.cn: 感到自卑就是在心里放一架梯子，然后站在低处。

examples.en: This cloth is inferior to the one we bought last year.
examples.cn: 这种布不如我们去年买的那种。

examples.en: He never spoke harshly to his inferiors.
examples.cn: 他从不对下属恶语相向。

examples.en: The inferior surface of the leaf is paler.
examples.cn: 叶子的下表面颜色更浅。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因费里尔」——因为要花费用，里面的东西就显得比较差。

root: 拉丁语 inferus（下面的）的比较级 inferior（更低的），与 superior 相对；同族词有 inferiority、inferno。

sensesIntro.en: The Latin comparative for lower spreads from physical position to rank, then to quality, to the people below you and finally to a private feeling of worth.
sensesIntro.cn: 表示「更低」的拉丁比较级从物理位置扩展到等级，再到质量、比自己级别低的人，最后到内心对自我价值的感受。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plain office on the floor below.
core.cn: 核心意象：楼下那间简陋的办公室。

branches.en: QUALITY LINE: not as good as the other.
branches.cn: 质量线：不如另一个。

branches.en: RANK LINE: lower in an organization.
branches.cn: 等级线：在组织中位置较低。

branches.en: POSITION LINE: literally underneath in anatomy.
branches.cn: 位置线：解剖学中字面意义上的下方。

branches.en: PEOPLE LINE: those who rank below you.
branches.cn: 人群线：级别低于你的人。

branches.en: SELF LINE: comparison turned into self-doubt.
branches.cn: 自我线：比较转化为自我怀疑。

intro.en: A Latin comparative adjective that still carries the -ior ending of its origin.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁比较级形容词，至今保留其来源的 -ior 词尾。

latinIntro.en: The family of inferus also gives infernal and inferno, all built on the idea of below.
latinIntro.cn: inferus 一族还产生 infernal 与 inferno，都建立在「在下」这一观念上。

definition_zh: 无限的；无穷的；极大的
definition_en: without limits or end in space, time or number
core_image: 一条向两端延伸到看不见尽头的直线
scene: 夜里抬头看天，星星数也数不完。The night sky seemed infinite to the child.
sceneCN: 这里 infinite 是「无限的」（第 1 个义项：没有边界或尽头）；句意是那片夜空在孩子看来是无限的。

pos.zh: 形容词：无限的；无穷的；极大的
名词（the infinite）：无限之物

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -ity，义为「无限；无穷」
加 -ly，义为「无限地；极大地」
去掉否定前缀，义为「有限的」
同出拉丁 finis，义为「不定式」

senses.title: Without end in space
senses.definition: having no boundary, so that it cannot be crossed
senses.definitionCN: 没有边界，无法穿越
senses.example: Space is thought to be infinite, or at least very large.
senses.exampleCN: 空间被认为是无限的，或者至少极大。
senses.why: In- means not and finis means end, so the word is literally endless.
senses.whyCN: in- 表示不，finis 表示终点，所以这个词字面就是没有尽头。

senses.title: Without end in number
senses.definition: too many to be counted, or continuing without a last term
senses.definitionCN: 多得无法计数，或没有最后一项
