senses.example: There are infinitely many numbers between one and two.
senses.exampleCN: 一与二之间有无限多个数。
senses.why: Mathematics turns the image of endless space into endless counting.
senses.whyCN: 数学把无尽空间的画面变成了无尽的计数。

senses.title: Without limit in degree
senses.definition: having no measurable limit, often used as a strong intensifier
senses.definitionCN: 没有可衡量的限度，常作很强的加强语
senses.example: You need infinite patience to teach small children.
senses.exampleCN: 教小孩子需要无限的耐心。
senses.why: Everyday speech borrows the word for anything that feels beyond measure.
senses.whyCN: 日常语言把这词借给任何感觉无法计量的东西。

senses.title: The boundless whole
senses.definition: what has no limits, used with the in philosophy
senses.definitionCN: 哲学中与 the 连用，指没有限度者
senses.example: The mystics spoke of union with the infinite.
senses.exampleCN: 神秘主义者谈到与无限合一。
senses.why: An adjective with the becomes an abstract noun for the whole of what is endless.
senses.whyCN: 形容词与 the 连用，成为指无尽整体的抽象名词。

senses.title: Endless in time
senses.definition: going on forever, with no end in time
senses.definitionCN: 永远持续，在时间上没有终点
senses.example: They imagined an infinite series of past days.
senses.exampleCN: 他们想象过去的日子是无限的系列。
senses.why: From space the word stretches to time, another kind of extent.
senses.whyCN: 从空间出发，这个词延伸到时间，这是另一种广延。

intro.en: Infinite joins Latin in-, not, to finitus, finished, from finis, end or boundary.
intro.cn: infinite 把拉丁否定 in- 加到 finitus（已结束的）上，后者出自 finis（终点、边界）。

items.en: Finis meant a boundary or end, as in the finish of a race.
items.cn: finis 意为边界或终点，如赛跑的终点。

items.en: Finitus, finished or limited, took the negative prefix to give infinitus.
items.cn: finitus（已结束的、有限的）加否定前缀，得到 infinitus。

items.en: The word entered English through French in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 这个词在十四世纪经法语进入英语。

items.en: Theology first used infinite of God, then mathematics took it over.
items.cn: 神学先用 infinite 形容上帝，随后数学接管了它。

items.en: The loose sense of very great became common in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 「极大」这一宽松义项在日常口语中普遍起来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the finis family; the near-meaning group holds words for what has no limit.
note.cn: 形近组收 finis 词族；近义组收表示无边无际的词。

entries.definition: The state of having no limit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「无限」，是本词的名词。
形容词，义为「有限的」，去掉否定前缀。

entries.definition: To state the exact meaning, to set limits.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「下定义」，本义是划定边界。
形容词，义为「无尽的」，最直白的说法。
形容词，义为「无边无际的」。
形容词，义为「无限制的」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks lock onto finis, the negative prefix and the mathematical picture of a number line.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子抓住 finis、否定前缀以及数轴的数学画面。

normal.en: In- means not, finis means end, so infinite is simply not ended.
normal.cn: in- 表示不，finis 表示终点，所以 infinite 就是没有终点。

normal.en: The same root gives finish, define and final: all about limits.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 finish、define、final，都与界限有关。

normal.en: Infinity is the noun, infinitely the adverb, finite the opposite.
normal.cn: infinity 是名词，infinitely 是副词，finite 是反义词。

normal.en: The infinity sign looks like a line with no end, the word made visible.
normal.cn: 无穷符号像一条没有尽头的线，是这个词的可见形式。

normal.en: Infinite patience is figurative, but the picture is still an endless length.
normal.cn: infinite patience 是比喻，但画面仍是一段无尽的长度。

abstract.en: Infinite is not a big number; it is the absence of a last one.
abstract.cn: infinite 不是一个大数，而是缺少那最后一个数。

abstract.en: A boundary is what finis means, so to be infinite is to be beyond all drawing of lines.
abstract.cn: finis 的意思是边界，所以无限就是超出一切划界。

abstract.en: The word makes the mind stretch until it can no longer finish the picture.
abstract.cn: 这个词让头脑不断延展，直到画不完那个画面。

examples.en: The universe may be finite or infinite; nobody knows.
examples.cn: 宇宙可能是有限的，也可能是无限的，无人知晓。

examples.en: She showed infinite patience with the new students.
examples.cn: 她对新来的学生表现出无限的耐心。

examples.en: An infinite series has no last term.
examples.cn: 无限级数没有最后一项。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因飞你特」——因为飞得特别远，才显得无穷无尽。

root: 拉丁否定前缀 in-（不）+ finitus（有限的），出自 finis（终点、边界）；同族词有 infinity、finite、define。

sensesIntro.en: From the literal absence of a boundary, infinite moves to endless counting, then to immeasurable degree, to the philosophical whole and to time without end.
sensesIntro.cn: 从字面上没有边界出发，infinite 走向无尽的计数，再到无法计量的程度、哲学上的整体，以及没有终点的时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight line running past both edges of the page.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条直线越过纸的两端。

branches.en: SPACE LINE: no edge can be reached.
branches.cn: 空间线：到不了任何边缘。

branches.en: NUMBER LINE: counting never stops.
branches.cn: 数量线：计数永不停止。

branches.en: DEGREE LINE: patience without measure.
branches.cn: 程度线：无法计量的耐心。

branches.en: WHOLE LINE: the infinite as a noun.
branches.cn: 整体线：作为名词的「无限」。

branches.en: TIME LINE: extent stretched into duration.
branches.cn: 时间线：广延拉长为持续。

intro.en: A negative prefix on an adjective of limits, the same formula behind countless English words.
intro.cn: 一个在「有限」形容词前的否定前缀，这一构式造出无数英语词。

latinIntro.en: The root finis, end, appears in final, finish, define and confine.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 finis（终点）见于 final、finish、define 与 confine。

definition_zh: 通货膨胀；通胀；充气；膨胀
definition_en: a general rise in prices, or the act of filling something with air
core_image: 气球被不断打气，越鼓越大，价格标签也跟着上涨
scene: 超市里同样的钱买到的东西一年比一年少。Rising prices have pushed inflation above five percent.
sceneCN: 这里 inflation 是「通货膨胀」（第 1 个义项：物价普遍上涨）；句意是物价上涨把通胀推高到百分之五以上。

pos.zh: 名词：通货膨胀；充气；膨胀

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ion，义为「使充气；使膨胀」
加 -ed，义为「充了气的；虚高的」
加 de-，义为「通货紧缩；放气」
加 -ary，义为「引起通胀的」

senses.title: A rise in prices
senses.definition: a general and continuing rise in the prices of goods and services
senses.definitionCN: 商品与服务价格的普遍持续上涨
senses.example: Inflation has made housing unaffordable for many.
senses.exampleCN: 通胀让许多人买不起住房。
senses.why: Money loses its buying power as prices swell, so the image of blowing up fits.
senses.whyCN: 物价膨胀时钱就失去购买力，所以「吹胀」的画面正合适。

senses.title: The act of filling with air
senses.definition: the process of filling something with air or gas
senses.definitionCN: 用空气或气体把某物充满的过程
senses.example: Inflation of the tyres should be checked monthly.
senses.exampleCN: 轮胎的充气情况应每月检查。
senses.why: This is the literal sense: something is blown into a container and swells.
senses.whyCN: 这是本义：东西被吹进容器，使它鼓起。

senses.title: Swelling of volume
senses.definition: an increase in size or volume, as of a balloon or a lung
senses.definitionCN: 尺寸或体积增大，如气球或肺
senses.example: The inflation of the lungs allows air to enter.
senses.exampleCN: 肺的扩张让空气得以进入。
senses.why: From a filled object the word moves to any increase in volume.
senses.whyCN: 从被充满的物体，这个词转向任何体积的增大。

senses.title: Language puffed up
senses.definition: the use of swollen or exaggerated language
senses.definitionCN: 使用浮夸或夸大的语言
senses.example: Critics objected to the inflation of his style.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者反对他文风的浮夸。
senses.why: Speech can be blown up too, and the word covers that puffiness.
senses.whyCN: 语言也能被吹胀，这个词同样涵盖那种浮夸。

senses.title: Inflation of numbers
senses.definition: an artificial increase in figures, such as grades or estimates
senses.definitionCN: 成绩或估价等人为的数值提高
senses.example: There were complaints about grade inflation at the college.
senses.exampleCN: 有人抱怨这所学院存在分数虚高。
senses.why: Anything puffed up without real substance is called inflated.
senses.whyCN: 凡是缺乏实质却被吹大的东西，都叫 inflated。

intro.en: Inflation comes from Latin inflatio, a blowing into, from inflare, in- plus flare, to blow.
intro.cn: inflation 来自拉丁语 inflatio（吹入），出自 inflare，即 in- 加 flare（吹气）。

items.en: Inflare meant to blow into or puff up, built on in- plus flare, to blow.
items.cn: inflare 意为吹入或吹胀，由 in- 加 flare（吹）构成。

items.en: Inflatio could describe a swollen style as well as filled objects.
items.cn: inflatio 既可描述被充满的物体，也可描述浮夸的文风。

items.en: The word came into English through French in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 这个词在中古时期经法语进入英语。

items.en: In the nineteenth century inflation was applied to paper money and prices.
items.cn: 十九世纪 inflation 被用于纸币与物价。

items.en: The economic sense became dominant in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 经济义在二十世纪成为主要含义。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the flare family; the near-meaning group holds words of price and volume change.
note.cn: 形近组收 flare 词族；近义组收描述价格与体积变化的词。

entries.definition: To fill with air or increase prices.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「充气；抬高」，是本词的原形。

entries.definition: A fall in prices, or the release of air.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「通货紧缩；放气」，与 inflation 相对。
形容词，义为「引起通胀的」。
名词，义为「肿胀；增大」，是体积方面最近的词。
名词，义为「扩张」，语气中性。

entries.definition: An increase in the cost of goods.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「物价上涨」，是通胀的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use flare, to blow, and the picture of money losing its puff.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 flare（吹气）以及钱越来越不值钱的画面。

normal.en: Flare means blow, so inflation is a blowing into, first of air, later of prices.
normal.cn: flare 意为吹，所以 inflation 就是「吹进去」，先是空气，后来是物价。

normal.en: Inflate is the verb, deflate the opposite, deflation the opposite noun.
normal.cn: inflate 是动词，deflate 是反义动词，deflation 是反义名词。

normal.en: A balloon and a currency share one picture: too much of what fills them.
normal.cn: 气球与货币共享一个画面：被填进的东西太多。

normal.en: The rate of inflation is the usual phrase in the news.
normal.cn: the rate of inflation 是新闻里常见的说法。

normal.en: Grade inflation borrows the economic word for marks that rise without effort.
normal.cn: grade inflation 借用了经济词，指不费力就上涨的分数。

abstract.en: Inflation makes money bigger and worth less at the same time.
abstract.cn: 通胀让钱看起来更大，同时也更不值钱。

abstract.en: The word says blown up, and what is blown up is soft inside.
abstract.cn: 这个词说的是「吹胀」，而被吹胀的东西里面是软的。

abstract.en: A balloon can be let down; money takes far longer to shrink back.
abstract.cn: 气球可以放气，钱要缩回去却慢得多。

examples.en: Inflation reached its highest level in ten years.
examples.cn: 通胀达到了十年来的最高水平。

examples.en: Check the inflation of your tyres before a long drive.
examples.cn: 长途驾驶前请检查轮胎的充气情况。

examples.en: Wages have not kept up with inflation.
examples.cn: 工资没有跟上通胀。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因费来神」——因为花费上涨，人人费神，钱来得神也留不住。

root: 拉丁语 inflare（吹入）= in-（进入）+ flare（吹气）；同族词有 inflate、deflation、inflationary。

sensesIntro.en: Inflation begins as blowing air into something, spreads to any swelling of volume, then to the swelling of language, of figures and finally of prices.
sensesIntro.cn: inflation 起初指把空气吹进某物，扩展到任何体积膨胀，然后延伸到浮夸的言辞、虚高的数字，最后是物价的膨胀。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balloon puffed up bigger and bigger.
core.cn: 核心意象：气球被打得越来越鼓。

branches.en: AIR LINE: gas is blown into a container.
branches.cn: 充气线：气体被吹进容器。

branches.en: VOLUME LINE: size grows with the air.
branches.cn: 体积线：尺寸随空气而增大。

branches.en: STYLE LINE: speech is puffed up too.
branches.cn: 文风线：语言同样被吹胀。

branches.en: FIGURE LINE: numbers rise without substance.
branches.cn: 数字线：数值虚增而无实质。

branches.en: MONEY LINE: prices swell until money shrinks.
branches.cn: 货币线：物价膨胀直到钱缩水。

intro.en: A noun in -ion from a Latin verb of blowing, used for air, style and money alike.
intro.cn: 以 -ion 结尾的名词，出自拉丁「吹」动词，兼用于空气、文风与货币。

latinIntro.en: The root flare, to blow, also gives inflate, flatulence and the English word blow's cousin in music.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 flare（吹）也产生 inflate、flatulence，以及音乐中表示吹奏的同源词。

definition_zh: 影响；作用；影响力；有影响的人或事
definition_en: the power to change how someone thinks or acts, or to affect events
core_image: 一股看不见的水流，把船慢慢带向旁边
scene: 老师的一句话，学生记了一辈子。His teacher had a lasting influence on his choice of career.
sceneCN: 这里 influence 是「影响」（第 1 个义项：对他人想法或选择的作用）；句意是他的老师对他的职业选择有持久的影响。

pos.zh: 名词：影响；影响力；有影响的人或事
动词：影响；对……起作用

derivatives.zh: 加 -ial，义为「有影响力的」
同出意大利语 influenza，义为「流行性感冒」
加 -ed，义为「受影响的」
加 un-，义为「未受影响的」

senses.title: Power over people
senses.definition: the power that one person or thing has to change others
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某物改变他人的力量
senses.example: Parents have a strong influence on young children.
senses.exampleCN: 父母对幼小的孩子有很强的影响。
senses.why: The Latin word was about an invisible fluid flowing in, and that is what influence feels like.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词原指流入的无形流体，而影响给人的感觉正是如此。

senses.title: A person or thing that affects
senses.definition: someone or something that changes others
senses.definitionCN: 改变他人的某个人或某件事
senses.example: She was the biggest influence on my writing.
senses.exampleCN: 她是对我写作影响最大的人。
senses.why: The abstract power is then attached to the person who carries it.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的力量随后被安放在携带它的人身上。

senses.title: The act of affecting events
senses.definition: the effect that conditions, money or groups have on events
senses.definitionCN: 条件、资金或团体对事件的作用
senses.example: The climate has an influence on what farmers can grow.
senses.exampleCN: 气候影响着农民能种什么。
senses.why: Beyond people, whole conditions can steer outcomes the same way.
senses.whyCN: 超越个人，整体条件也以同样的方式左右结果。

senses.title: To affect someone
senses.definition: to change the way someone thinks or behaves
senses.definitionCN: 改变某人的想法或行为
senses.example: Advertising influences what we buy.
senses.exampleCN: 广告影响着我们买什么。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb keeps the same picture of something flowing in.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词，仍是某种东西流进来的画面。

senses.title: Political or social power
senses.definition: the ability to affect decisions in public life
senses.definitionCN: 影响公共决策的能力
senses.example: The group used its influence to block the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 该团体动用它的影响力阻止了这项计划。
senses.why: In public affairs the word names the practical power behind decisions.
senses.whyCN: 在公共事务中，这个词指决策背后的实际力量。

intro.en: Influence comes from Medieval Latin influentia, a flowing in, from influere, in- plus fluere, to flow.
intro.cn: influence 来自中世纪拉丁语 influentia（流入），出自 influere，即 in- 加 fluere（流动）。

items.en: Fluere meant to flow, and influere meant to flow into.
items.cn: fluere 意为流动，influere 意为流入。

items.en: Astrologers spoke of influentia, an invisible power flowing from the stars into people.
items.cn: 占星家谈 influentia，即从星辰流入人体的无形力量。

items.en: The word entered English through French in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 这个词在十四世纪经法语进入英语。

items.en: When astrology faded, the word kept the sense of unseen power over people.
items.cn: 占星术衰落之后，这个词保留了「无形支配力」的含义。

items.en: The verb use developed later, from the same noun, in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 动词用法较晚，在十七世纪由同一名词发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the fluere family; the near-meaning group holds words of power over others.
note.cn: 形近组收 fluere 词族；近义组收描述对他人的支配力。

entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有影响力的」。

entries.definition: A virus that spreads like an influence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「流行性感冒」，同出意大利语 influenza。
名词或形容词，义为「流体」，与 fluere 同源。

entries.definition: A change produced by a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「效果」，强调结果。
名词，义为「影响；冲击」，语气更强。

entries.definition: The ability to make things happen.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「权力；力量」，是更宽泛的说法。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of flowing water, then attach the word to teachers and advertising.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子保留流水的画面，再把词与老师、广告相连。

normal.en: Fluere means flow, so influence is literally something flowing into you.
normal.cn: fluere 意为流动，所以 influence 字面上就是有东西流进你身上。

normal.en: The -ence ending makes a noun, and influential is its adjective.
normal.cn: -ence 词尾构成名词，influential 是其形容词。

normal.en: Have an influence on is the standard frame, with on rather than to.
normal.cn: have an influence on 是标准框架，用 on 而不是 to。

normal.en: Under the influence of means being steered while in that state.
normal.cn: under the influence of 意为处在那种状态下被左右。

normal.en: Influenza got its name because people thought the stars sent it flowing in.
normal.cn: influenza 得名是因为人们以为星辰把它送了下来。

abstract.en: Influence is an invisible current: nothing is pushed, yet the boat moves.
abstract.cn: 影响是一道看不见的水流：没有人推，船却动了。

abstract.en: To influence is to change another without touching, which is the quietest form of power.
abstract.cn: 影响是不接触就改变他人，这是最安静的力量形式。

abstract.en: The word once belonged to the stars, and it still suggests something above pouring down.
abstract.cn: 这个词曾属于星辰，至今仍暗示有东西自高处倾下。

examples.en: The book had a strong influence on young readers.
examples.cn: 这本书对年轻读者有很大影响。

examples.en: Do not let bad company influence your choices.
examples.cn: 不要让坏朋友影响你的选择。

examples.en: He used his influence to help the little school.
examples.cn: 他动用自己的影响力帮助那所小学校。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因福露恩死」——因为福气露了，恩情至死都在影响着他。

root: 中世纪拉丁语 influentia（流入）= in-（进入）+ fluere（流动）；同族词有 influential、fluent、fluid。

sensesIntro.en: From an astrological fluid flowing in, influence moves to power over people, then to the person who has it, to effects on events and finally to a verb of affecting.
sensesIntro.cn: 从占星术里流入的流体出发，influence 走向对人的支配力、有这种力的人、对事件的作用，最后成为表示影响他人的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unseen current pushing a boat sideways.
core.cn: 核心意象：看不见的水流把船推向一侧。

branches.en: PERSON LINE: one person's power over another.
branches.cn: 人际线：一个人对另一个人的力量。

branches.en: SOURCE LINE: the one who carries that power.
branches.cn: 来源线：携带这种力量的人。

branches.en: EVENT LINE: climate or money steers results.
branches.cn: 事件线：气候或资金左右结果。

branches.en: ACTION LINE: the noun becomes a verb.
branches.cn: 动作线：名词转为动词。

branches.en: PUBLIC LINE: power that reaches decisions.
branches.cn: 公共线：能影响决策的力量。

intro.en: A noun of flowing, whose -ence ending also appears in fluent and fluid.
intro.cn: 一个表示流动的名词，其 -ence 词尾也见于 fluent 与 fluid。

latinIntro.en: The root fluere, to flow, gives fluent, fluid, flux and the medical influenza.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 fluere（流动）产生 fluent、fluid、flux 以及医学词 influenza。

items.meaning: an outbreak once blamed on stars

definition_zh: 有影响力的；有势力的；有很大影响的
definition_en: having the power to affect people, decisions or events
core_image: 一个人说话，满屋子的人立刻改变主意
scene: 小镇上的报纸没人敢小看。The local paper has become influential far beyond the town.
sceneCN: 这里 influential 是「有影响力的」（第 1 个义项：能影响他人或决定）；句意是这家地方报纸的影响力已远及镇外。

pos.zh: 形容词：有影响力的；有势力的；有很大影响的

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ial，义为「影响」
加 -ly，义为「有影响地」
加否定前缀，义为「无影响力的」
同根词，义为「流行性感冒」

senses.title: Able to affect people
senses.definition: able to change how others think or act
senses.definitionCN: 能改变他人的想法或行为
senses.example: She became one of the most influential teachers in the school.
senses.exampleCN: 她成了学校里最有影响力的老师之一。
senses.why: The -ial ending simply turns influence into a quality someone has.
senses.whyCN: -ial 词尾只是把 influence 变成某人所具备的性质。

senses.title: Able to affect decisions
senses.definition: having power in politics, business or public life
senses.definitionCN: 在政治、商业或公共生活中拥有力量
senses.example: The committee is influential in local politics.
senses.exampleCN: 这个委员会在地方政治中很有影响力。
senses.why: Power over outcomes, not just opinions, is the second step.
senses.whyCN: 对结果而不只是对意见的支配力，是这个形容词的第二步。

senses.title: A work that shaped others
senses.definition: said of a book, idea or event that changed a whole field
senses.definitionCN: 指改变了整个领域的书、思想或事件
senses.example: This was an influential book on how children learn.
senses.exampleCN: 这是一本关于儿童如何学习的深有影响的书。
senses.why: Things can carry influence too, especially works that others follow.
senses.whyCN: 事物也能携带影响力，尤其是被后人效仿的作品。

senses.title: Having many connections
senses.definition: having wealth or friends who can make things happen
senses.definitionCN: 拥有财富或能办事的人脉
senses.example: His family is influential in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 他家在城里很有势力。
senses.why: From real effect the word slides to social weight and connections.
senses.whyCN: 从实际作用出发，这个词滑向社会分量与人脉。

intro.en: Influential is an English adjective formed on influence, from Medieval Latin influentia, a flowing in.
intro.cn: influential 是在 influence 上构成的英语形容词，后者出自中世纪拉丁语 influentia（流入）。

items.en: Influere meant to flow into, from in- plus fluere, to flow.
items.cn: influere 意为流入，由 in- 加 fluere（流动）构成。

items.en: Influentia named the invisible power believed to flow from the stars.
items.cn: influentia 指人们相信从星辰流入的无形力量。

items.en: The noun reached English through French in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 这个名词在十四世纪经法语进入英语。

items.en: The suffix -ial was attached to make an adjective in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 十七世纪加上后缀 -ial 构成形容词。

items.en: Influential spread widely with talk of influential people and papers in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪谈有影响的人物与报纸，influential 广泛流行。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the fluere family; the near-meaning group holds adjectives of power.
note.cn: 形近组收 fluere 词族；近义组收表示力量与地位的形容词。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「影响」，是本词的来源。

entries.definition: A virus that once was blamed on the stars.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「流感」，同出意大利语 influenza。

entries.definition: In a way that has effect.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「有影响地」。
形容词，义为「强大的」，更笼统。
形容词，义为「重要的」，不必然指影响他人。
形容词，义为「显著的」，强调分量。

normalIntro.en: The hooks connect the adjective to its noun and to the flowing picture behind both.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把形容词与它的名词以及背后的流水画面相连。

normal.en: Influence plus -ial gives an adjective: full of influence.
normal.cn: influence 加 -ial 得形容词：充满影响力的。

normal.en: Influential is almost always used of people, papers and books, not of weather.
normal.cn: influential 几乎总用于人、报纸与书，而不用来形容天气。

normal.en: Influential in politics means able to steer decisions.
normal.cn: influential in politics 意为能左右决策。

normal.en: The spelling keeps the -flu- of flow, so the word still sounds like water.
normal.cn: 拼写保留流动的 -flu-，这个词听起来仍像水。

normal.en: More influential and most influential handle the comparison.
normal.cn: more influential 与 most influential 承担比较级与最高级。

abstract.en: An influential person is a river others quietly follow.
abstract.cn: 有影响力的人是一条别人默默顺着走的河。

abstract.en: Influence is measured backwards: we see it only in what changed.
abstract.cn: 影响力的度量是回望的：我们只在改变了的东西里看见它。

abstract.en: The word means pouring in, and power that pours never stays in one place.
abstract.cn: 这个词意为灌入，而倾注的力量从不只停在一处。

examples.en: He was an influential member of the committee.
examples.cn: 他是委员会里很有影响力的成员。

examples.en: The report proved influential in changing the law.
examples.cn: 这份报告在改变法律方面被证明很有影响。

examples.en: Few writers have been as influential as she was.
examples.cn: 很少有作家像她那样影响深远。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因福露恩少」——因为福气与恩情露得少，才更要靠影响力说话。

root: influence（影响）+ -ial（形容词后缀）；词根为拉丁 fluere（流动）。

sensesIntro.en: Influential turns the flowing-in power into a quality: able to change people, then decisions, then whole fields, and finally social weight.
sensesIntro.cn: influential 把流入的力量变成一种性质：能改变人，然后是决策、整个领域，最后是社会分量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a speaker who changes the room in one sentence.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话就让满屋转向的发言者。

branches.en: PEOPLE LINE: able to change minds.
branches.cn: 人际线：能改变人心。

branches.en: DECISION LINE: able to steer outcomes.
branches.cn: 决策线：能左右结果。

branches.en: WORKS LINE: books and ideas that reshape a field.
branches.cn: 作品线：重塑一个领域的书与思想。

branches.en: STATUS LINE: wealth and connections that carry weight.
branches.cn: 地位线：有分量的财富与人脉。

branches.en: POWER LINE: one unseen force, two directions.
branches.cn: 力量线：同一股无形之力，两个方向。

intro.en: An adjective in -ial formed on the noun of flowing in.
intro.cn: 一个以 -ial 结尾、由「流入」名词构成的形容词。

latinIntro.en: The root fluere, to flow, gives fluent, fluid, flux and influenza.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 fluere（流动）产生 fluent、fluid、flux 与 influenza。

definition_zh: 通知；告知；举报；影响（风格）
definition_en: to tell someone officially or clearly about something
core_image: 一封信被送到门口，里面写着要知道的事
scene: 车站的广播突然响起来。Please inform the office if you change your address.
sceneCN: 这里 inform 是「告知」（第 1 个义项：把情况正式告诉别人）；句意是如果改变地址，请告知办公室。

pos.zh: 动词：通知；告知；举报
及物：使了解；赋予特征

derivatives.zh: 加 -ation，义为「信息；消息」
加 -ed，义为「了解情况的」
加 -ative，义为「提供有用信息的」
加 -ant，义为「提供消息的人」

senses.title: To tell officially
senses.definition: to give someone facts they need to know
senses.definitionCN: 把对方需要知道的事实告诉他
senses.example: Please inform us of any change of plan.
senses.exampleCN: 计划如有变动请告知我们。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to give shape, and giving shape to someone's knowledge is informing them.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「赋予形状」，而给一个人的知识赋予形状就是告知他。

senses.title: To report to authorities
senses.definition: to give information about wrongdoing to the police or officials
senses.definitionCN: 向警方或官方提供有关违法行为的消息
senses.example: He informed on his partners to save himself.
senses.exampleCN: 为了自保，他举报了合伙人。
senses.why: Information given to power becomes a report, and the verb narrows to that act.
senses.whyCN: 交给权力的信息就是举报，动词于是收窄到这个动作。

senses.title: To shape a decision
senses.definition: to give the knowledge that shapes a choice or work
senses.definitionCN: 提供塑造选择或作品的知识
senses.example: The survey will inform future policy.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查将为今后的政策提供依据。
senses.why: Since inform meant to give shape, it also describes knowledge shaping decisions.
senses.whyCN: 由于 inform 本义是赋予形状，它也用来描述知识塑造决策。

senses.title: To fill with a quality
senses.definition: to give a work or action its special character
senses.definitionCN: 赋予作品或行为以特有的性质
senses.example: A quiet sadness informs the whole novel.
senses.exampleCN: 一种静默的忧伤贯穿整部小说。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: a form is breathed into a thing.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：把一种形态注入事物之中。

senses.title: To keep informed
senses.definition: to give people continuing news, used in keep informed
senses.definitionCN: 持续向人提供消息，见于 keep informed
senses.example: Keep me informed about the results.
senses.exampleCN: 结果如何随时告诉我。
senses.why: Continuous telling becomes a fixed phrase about staying up to date.
senses.whyCN: 持续的告知形成固定说法，表示保持在最新状态。

intro.en: Inform comes from Latin informare, to shape or give form, from in- plus forma, form.
intro.cn: inform 来自拉丁语 informare（赋予形状），由 in- 加 forma（形状）构成。

items.en: Forma meant shape, and informare meant to give shape to something.
items.cn: forma 意为形状，informare 意为给某物赋予形状。

items.en: The verb also meant to instruct, since teaching shapes the mind.
items.cn: 这个动词也指教导，因为教学塑造心灵。

items.en: The word came into English through French with the sense of teaching.
items.cn: 这个词经法语进入英语，带有教导之义。

items.en: By the sixteenth century inform meant to tell facts.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，inform 意为告知事实。

items.en: The sense of giving character survived in literary descriptions.
items.cn: 「赋予特征」的义项在文学描写中留存下来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the forma family; the near-meaning group holds verbs of telling.
note.cn: 形近组收 forma 词族；近义组收告知类动词。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「信息」，是本词的名词形式。
形容词，义为「提供有用信息的」。
名词，义为「形状；表格」，是词根本身。
动词，义为「通知」，语气更正式。
动词，义为「告诉」，最日常的说法。
动词，义为「宣布」，面向公众。

normalIntro.en: The hooks lean on forma and on the family of nouns and adjectives built from inform.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 forma 以及由 inform 构成的名词形容词词族。

normal.en: Forma means shape, so to inform is to shape what someone knows.
normal.cn: forma 意为形状，所以 inform 就是塑造别人的认知。

normal.en: Inform someone of something uses of, not about, in careful writing.
normal.cn: inform someone of something 在正式写作中用 of 而不用 about。

normal.en: Keep me informed is the fixed phrase for staying up to date.
normal.cn: keep me informed 是表示随时知情的固定说法。

normal.en: Informative adds -ive: a talk that gives you a lot of facts.
normal.cn: informative 加 -ive：一次给你很多事实的讲座。

normal.en: Inform on someone means to report them, a very different direction.
normal.cn: inform on someone 意为举报某人，方向大不相同。

abstract.en: To inform is to pour facts into a mould the mind already has.
abstract.cn: 告知是把事实倒进心里已有的模子。

abstract.en: Knowledge has a shape, and news is what reshapes it.
abstract.cn: 知识有形状，消息就是重塑它的东西。

abstract.en: The word joins form and news: what we are told gives form to what we think.
abstract.cn: 这个词把形状与消息连在一起：我们被告知的东西塑造着我们怎么想。

examples.en: The school will inform parents of any change.
examples.cn: 学校会把任何变动通知家长。

examples.en: He informed the police about the broken window.
examples.cn: 他把窗户被打破的事报告了警方。

examples.en: Good research should inform the final decision.
examples.cn: 好的研究应当为最终决定提供依据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因佛母」——因为佛母显灵，消息要赶紧通知众人。

root: 拉丁语 informare（赋予形状）= in-（进入）+ forma（形状）；同族词有 information、informative、form。

sensesIntro.en: Inform starts as giving shape, becomes teaching, then telling facts, and branches into reporting to the police and shaping decisions or works.
sensesIntro.cn: inform 起初是赋予形状，继而指教导，再变为告知事实，并分支为向警方举报，以及为决策或作品提供形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a letter at the door with the facts inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：门口一封信，里面装着要知道的事。

branches.en: TELL LINE: facts given to the person who needs them.
branches.cn: 告知线：把事实交给需要的人。

branches.en: REPORT LINE: information handed to power.
branches.cn: 举报线：信息被交给权力。

branches.en: DECISION LINE: knowledge shapes a choice.
branches.cn: 决策线：知识塑造选择。

branches.en: CHARACTER LINE: a quality shapes a work.
branches.cn: 特征线：某种性质塑造作品。

branches.en: CONTINUITY LINE: staying informed over time.
branches.cn: 持续线：随时间保持知情。

intro.en: A Latin verb of shaping whose family covers news, teaching and form itself.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语「赋形」动词，其词族覆盖消息、教导与形状本身。

latinIntro.en: The root forma, shape, gives form, format, reform and information.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 forma（形状）产生 form、format、reform 与 information。

definition_zh: 非正式的；不拘礼的；随意的；口语的
definition_en: relaxed and friendly, not following official rules or ceremony
core_image: 脱下西装换上T恤，大家坐在沙发上聊天
scene: 聚会没有主持，也没有发言顺序。It was an informal dinner, so nobody dressed up.
sceneCN: 这里 informal 是「非正式的」（第 1 个义项：不按礼节与规矩进行）；句意那是顿非正式的晚餐，所以没人盛装打扮。

pos.zh: 形容词：非正式的；不拘礼的；随意的

derivatives.zh: 义为「正式地」，去掉否定前缀后加 -ly
加 -ity，义为「非正式；随意」
加 -ly，义为「非正式地」
去掉否定前缀，义为「正式的」

senses.title: Relaxed in manner
senses.definition: easy and friendly rather than stiff and polite
senses.definitionCN: 轻松友好，而非拘谨客套
senses.example: The interview felt informal and friendly.
senses.exampleCN: 那次面谈感觉随意而友好。
senses.why: In- removes the rules of form, so the word means without ceremony.
senses.whyCN: in- 去掉了形式的规矩，所以这个词意为「没有礼节」。

senses.title: Not official
senses.definition: not arranged according to official rules
senses.definitionCN: 不按官方规定安排
senses.example: They reached an informal agreement over lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在午餐时达成了一项非正式协议。
senses.why: Something can be real without being official, and that is the gap this word fills.
senses.whyCN: 事情可以真实却不正式，这个词正好填补这个空档。

senses.title: Everyday in style
senses.definition: suitable for ordinary rather than special occasions
senses.definitionCN: 适合日常场合而非特殊场合
senses.example: Informal clothes are fine for the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 这次旅行穿便装就可以。
senses.why: Dress follows ceremony, so clothes too are called informal.
senses.whyCN: 着装跟随礼节，因此衣服也被称为 informal。

senses.title: Spoken in everyday language
senses.definition: using the words people use in ordinary talk
senses.definitionCN: 使用人们日常交谈中的词语
senses.example: Gonna is an informal form of going to.
senses.exampleCN: gonna 是 going to 的口语形式。
senses.why: Language has registers, and the word marks the relaxed one.
senses.whyCN: 语言有语体之分，这个词标示轻松的那一端。

senses.title: Outside the official system
senses.definition: happening outside official structures, as of work or trade
senses.definitionCN: 在官方体系之外进行，如工作或交易
senses.example: Many people work in the informal economy.
senses.exampleCN: 许多人在非正规经济中工作。
senses.why: From manners the word reaches economics, where no contract is registered.
senses.whyCN: 从举止出发，这个词延伸到经济学中无登记合同的地带。

intro.en: Informal puts the Latin negative in- on formal, from Latin formalis, of a form, from forma.
intro.cn: informal 把拉丁否定 in- 加在 formal 上，后者出自拉丁 formalis（属于形式的），源自 forma。

items.en: Forma meant shape, and formalis meant belonging to a form or pattern.
items.cn: forma 意为形状，formalis 意为属于某种形式或范式的。

items.en: Formal later covered what follows set rules and ceremony.
items.cn: formal 后来涵盖遵循既定规则与礼节的事物。

items.en: Formal entered English in the fourteenth century from Latin.
items.cn: formal 在十四世纪由拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: Informal was formed with in- to name what is free of ceremony.
items.cn: informal 加 in- 而构成，用来指不受礼节约束的事物。

items.en: The sociological phrase informal economy spread in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 社会学用语 informal economy 在二十世纪流行。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the forma family; the near-meaning group holds words for a relaxed manner.
note.cn: 形近组收 forma 词族；近义组收表示轻松不拘的词。

entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「正式的」，与 informal 相对。
名词，义为「非正式；随意」。
名词，义为「信息」，只是拼写相近，词源不同。
形容词，义为「随意的」，最接近的日常词。
形容词，义为「非官方的」，强调合法性。
形容词，义为「放松的」，强调人的状态。

normalIntro.en: The hooks pair informal with formal, then mark the -al ending and the social uses.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 informal 与 formal 对照，再点出 -al 词尾与社会场景。

normal.en: In- means not, so informal is simply the reverse of formal.
normal.cn: in- 表示不，所以 informal 就是 formal 的反面。

normal.en: Both words keep the -al ending of the Latin adjective formalis.
normal.cn: 两词都保留拉丁形容词 formalis 的 -al 词尾。

normal.en: Informal economy names work that no office records.
normal.cn: informal economy 指没有机构登记的劳动。

normal.en: An informal chat is shorter and friendlier than a formal meeting.
normal.cn: an informal chat 比正式会议更短更亲切。

normal.en: The noun is informality, not informalness.
normal.cn: 名词是 informality，而不是 informalness。

abstract.en: Formal is a costume; informal is the person inside it taking it off.
abstract.cn: formal 是一套服装，informal 是里面的人把它脱下。

abstract.en: Informatity is trust expressed in manner: no need for ceremony.
abstract.cn: 非正式是在举止里表达信任：不必走礼数。

abstract.en: The word measures distance: the less ceremony, the closer the people.
abstract.cn: 这个词衡量距离：礼节越少，人越近。

examples.en: The meeting was informal and everyone spoke freely.
examples.cn: 那次会议很随意，大家畅所欲言。

examples.en: You can wear informal clothes to the party.
examples.cn: 参加这个聚会可以穿便装。

examples.en: They made an informal arrangement to share the cost.
examples.cn: 他们非正式地约定分摊费用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因佛帽」——因为佛帽一摘，人就显得不拘礼节、很随意。

root: 拉丁否定前缀 in-（不）+ formal（正式的），formal 出自拉丁 formalis（形式的）。

sensesIntro.en: Informal simply removes form from formal: relaxed manners, unofficial deals, everyday clothes, spoken language and work outside official systems.
sensesIntro.cn: informal 只是把 formal 的「形式」去掉：轻松的举止、非官方约定、日常衣着、口语，以及官方体系外的劳动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ties loosened, jackets off, people talking freely.
core.cn: 核心意象：松开领带、脱下外套，人们随意交谈。

branches.en: MANNER LINE: easy and friendly behaviour.
branches.cn: 举止线：轻松友好的行为。

branches.en: OFFICIAL LINE: real but not registered.
branches.cn: 官方线：真实但未登记。

branches.en: DRESS LINE: clothes for ordinary days.
branches.cn: 衣着线：日常穿着。

branches.en: LANGUAGE LINE: the spoken register.
branches.cn: 语言线：口语语体。

branches.en: SYSTEM LINE: activity outside formal structures.
branches.cn: 体系线：正式结构之外的活动。

intro.en: A negative prefix on an adjective of form, the pattern behind many English opposites.
intro.cn: 一个加在「形式的」形容词前的否定前缀，构成英语中大量反义词。

latinIntro.en: The root forma, shape, gives formal, format, reform and uniform.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 forma（形状）产生 formal、format、reform 与 uniform。

definition_zh: 信息；资料；消息；情报
definition_en: facts or details about someone or something
core_image: 抽屉里一叠整理好的卡片，每张写着一件事
scene: 出发前先查清路线和时刻。We need more information about the trains before we book.
sceneCN: 这里 information 是「信息、资料」（第 1 个义项：关于某事的事实）；句意是订票之前我们需要更多关于列车的信息。

pos.zh: 名词：信息；资料；消息；情报（不可数）

forms.label: 无变化（不可数名词，无复数）

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ation，义为「通知；告知」
加 -ive，义为「信息量大的」
加 -ed，义为「知情的」
加 -al，义为「信息性的」

senses.title: Facts about something
senses.definition: facts and details about a subject
senses.definitionCN: 关于某个主题的事实与细节
senses.example: The leaflet gives information about opening times.
senses.exampleCN: 这份传单提供了开放时间的信息。
senses.why: The noun names what informing delivers: knowledge shaped into usable facts.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名告知所交付的东西：被整理成可用事实的知识。

senses.title: News about people
senses.definition: news or details about a person
senses.definitionCN: 关于某人的消息与细节
senses.example: Police are still collecting information about the incident.
senses.exampleCN: 警方仍在收集关于这一事件的消息。
senses.why: From subjects the word turns to persons and events.
senses.whyCN: 从主题出发，这个词转向人物与事件。

senses.title: Data in a system
senses.definition: data stored and processed by computers or organizations
senses.definitionCN: 计算机或机构存储与处理的数据
senses.example: The information is kept on a secure server.
senses.exampleCN: 这些信息保存在一台安全的服务器上。
senses.why: Modern technology makes information something stored rather than remembered.
senses.whyCN: 现代技术让信息成为被存储的东西，而不再是被记住的东西。

senses.title: Intelligence for decisions
senses.definition: facts gathered for official or military use
senses.definitionCN: 为官方或军事用途收集的事实
senses.example: The agency gathered information on the group for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个机构多年来收集该团体的情报。
senses.why: Information gathered for power takes the name intelligence, but the noun stays the same.
senses.whyCN: 为权力收集的信息叫作情报，但用的仍是这个名词。

senses.title: The act of informing
senses.definition: the act of giving someone facts, mainly in older use
senses.definitionCN: 把事实告知他人的行为，多见于较老用法
senses.example: Thank you for your information about the road closure.
senses.exampleCN: 谢谢你告知道路封闭的消息。
senses.why: The -ation ending keeps the old sense of the action as well as its result.
senses.whyCN: -ation 词尾既保留动作的旧义，也保留其结果。

intro.en: Information comes from Latin informatio, a shaping or an outline, from informare, to give form.
intro.cn: information 来自拉丁语 informatio（塑造、勾勒），出自 informare（赋予形状）。

items.en: Informatio meant the act of giving shape or forming an idea.
items.cn: informatio 意为赋予形状或形成观念的行为。

items.en: It also named an outline, the shape of a plan or a case.
items.cn: 它也指轮廓，即某项计划或案件的概要。

items.en: The word passed into French and then into English in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 这个词经法语在中古时期进入英语。

items.en: Informatio became information, meaning instruction and later news.
items.cn: informatio 变为 information，先指教导，后指消息。

items.en: In the twentieth century information became a technical word for data.
items.cn: 二十世纪 information 成为指数据的技术词。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the inform family; the near-meaning group holds words for facts and news.
note.cn: 形近组收 inform 词族；近义组收事实与消息类名词。

entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「告知」，是本词的原形。
形容词，义为「信息量大的」。
名词，义为「转变」，与 form 同根。
名词，义为「数据」，偏技术意味。
名词，义为「新闻」，强调新近发生。

entries.definition: What a person understands and knows.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「知识」，比 information 更内在。

normalIntro.en: The hooks note the -ation ending, the uncountable grammar and the split from data and news.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子留意 -ation 词尾、不可数语法，以及与 data、news 的区别。

normal.en: Inform plus -ation makes the noun of the thing given when you inform.
normal.cn: inform 加 -ation 构成名词，指告知时给出的东西。

normal.en: Information is uncountable: a piece of information, never informations.
normal.cn: information 不可数：a piece of information，绝不说 informations。

normal.en: Information technology puts the word at the centre of modern work.
normal.cn: information technology 把这个词放在现代工作的中心。

normal.en: Knowledge lives in a person, information lives in a note or a file.
normal.cn: knowledge 住在人心里，information 住在便条或文件里。

normal.en: The old sense survives in thank you for your information.
normal.cn: 旧义仍留在 thank you for your information 这样的说法里。

abstract.en: Information is form given to facts so that others can carry them.
abstract.cn: 信息是给事实赋予的形状，让别人也能带走。

abstract.en: The word once meant shaping, and a mind is still shaped by what it receives.
abstract.cn: 这个词曾指塑造，而头脑至今仍被它接收的东西塑造。

abstract.en: Too much information is not knowledge; it is only more shape.
abstract.cn: 信息太多并不等于知识，只是更多形状而已。

examples.en: Please send me information about the course.
examples.cn: 请把关于这门课程的信息发给我。

examples.en: He gave the police information about the car.
examples.cn: 他向警方提供了关于那辆车的信息。

examples.en: All personal information is kept safe.
examples.cn: 所有个人信息都被妥善保存。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因佛没神」——因为拜佛没显灵，只好自己收集信息资料。

root: inform（告知）+ -ation（名词后缀）；词根为拉丁 forma（形状）。

sensesIntro.en: Information keeps the old sense of shaping while becoming facts about subjects, news about people, stored data and gathered intelligence.
sensesIntro.cn: information 保留「塑造」的旧义，同时演变为关于主题的事实、关于人物的消息、存储的数据以及收集的情报。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of cards each holding one fact.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠卡片，每张写着一件事实。

branches.en: FACT LINE: details about a subject.
branches.cn: 事实线：关于某主题的细节。

branches.en: NEWS LINE: what is said about people.
branches.cn: 消息线：关于人们的说法。

branches.en: DATA LINE: facts stored in systems.
branches.cn: 数据线：存于系统中的事实。

branches.en: POWER LINE: facts gathered for decisions.
branches.cn: 权力线：为决策收集的事实。

branches.en: SHAPING LINE: the act of informing and what it leaves.
branches.cn: 塑造线：告知的行为及其留下的东西。

intro.en: The noun of informing, built with the productive suffix -ation.
intro.cn: 表示告知的名词，由能产后缀 -ation 构成。

latinIntro.en: The root forma, shape, gives formation, format and transformation.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 forma（形状）产生 formation、format 与 transformation。
